Application areas include elderly care workforce well-being, family-centered care for children with cerebral palsy, digital technology in a diabetes transition clinic, and the role of champions in quality improvement.

name: Victoria Vatsvåg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Victoria Vatsvåg studies medical education in point-of-care ultrasound, focusing on whether teaching delivered remotely through videoconferencing can match in-person instruction. Her work compares student groups in a prehospital critical care program using pre- and post-course tests of knowledge, image interpretation, scanning technique and clinical decision-making. The findings relate to telemedicine and training in settings with physical distancing or long distances.

name: Vilde M. Thomseth
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Vilde M. Thomseth studies the retina and ocular surface in clinical ophthalmology, focusing on how repeated anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for neovascular age-related macular degeneration affect tear film, meibomian glands, redness and tear cytokines, and on recovery after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment surgery. Her work uses prospective and retrospective observational designs, with the fellow eye as control, along with imaging such as swept-source and en face optical coherence tomography, infrared homography and keratography, plus visual function testing and tear assays. She also reports on the long-term incidence of retinal detachment in Western Norway and on retinal and choroidal changes after reattachment.

name: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel studies prehospital emergency and trauma medicine in Austria, with a focus on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (including traumatic and paediatric cases), physician-staffed ground and helicopter emergency services, and the staffing and triage of emergency calls. His work uses retrospective cohort analyses, nationwide audits, Delphi consensus processes and literature reviews, and also covers spinal cord injury epidemiology and drug therapies for haemorrhagic shock and severe traumatic brain injury.

name: Anders Blilie
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Anders Blilie develops and validates deep learning systems for digital pathology of prostate cancer, covering diagnosis, Gleason grading and detection of cribriform morphology in whole-slide images of biopsies. The work tests how well these models hold up across laboratories, scanners and populations, including a Middle Eastern cohort, and examines technical factors such as tissue detection, scanner colour calibration and conformal prediction for flagging unreliable outputs. Further publications cover a public biopsy image dataset, a pre-registered validation protocol, AI use to reduce immunohistochemistry staining, and biobanking protocols for prostatectomy tissue.

name: Caroline Guldberg Fugelli
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Caroline Guldberg Fugelli studies how multidisciplinary simulation training affects care for acute stroke patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy, with a focus on anaesthesia in non-operating room settings. Her work combines pre-post interventional studies of clinical workflow, anaesthetic management and patient outcomes with a qualitative focus group study of team members' training experiences. The research is applied in hospital stroke care and informs how simulation programmes and faculty are designed.

name: Frederikke Buskov
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Frederikke Buskov studies newborn care around the time of birth, covering resuscitation in the delivery room and the care of preterm infants in neonatal intensive care. Her work uses randomized trials, prospective observational studies, video analysis, dry-electrode ECG heart rate data and systematic review methods to examine heart rate monitoring, ventilation, tactile stimulation, pulse oximetry and umbilical pH. It also covers early skin-to-skin contact for preterm infants and the methodological problem of selection bias in a resuscitation trial that relied on video recordings.

name: Hanne Pike
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Hanne Pike studies newborn care, covering immediate parent–infant skin-to-skin contact for very preterm infants and the resuscitation of newborns at birth. Her work uses randomised clinical trials to assess thermoregulation, stress responses, mother–infant cortisol patterns and neurodevelopment, and uses observational and video-recording studies to document resuscitation practice in Norway and rural Tanzania. Application areas include neonatal intensive care, delivery-room heart rate monitoring with dry-electrode ECG and pulse oximetry, and adherence to resuscitation guidelines.

name: Karoline Lode-Kolz
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Karoline Lode-Kolz studies immediate skin-to-skin contact between parents and very preterm infants in neonatal intensive care, mainly through secondary analyses of the multicentre randomised IPISTOSS trial in Sweden and Norway, and a systematic review of trials in high-resource settings. Outcomes examined include cardiorespiratory stability, thermoregulation, stress response and cortisol synchrony, mother-infant interaction, parental depression and anxiety, and motor, cognitive and language development up to two years. The work uses clinical trial methods, standardised behavioural and developmental assessments, salivary cortisol sampling and evidence synthesis to inform neonatal care practice.

name: Malin Knutsen Glette
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Malin Knutsen Glette studies resilience, leadership, patient safety and staff wellbeing in healthcare, with a focus on elderly care, nursing homes, home care and rural primary care. Her work uses systematic, integrative and scoping reviews, qualitative interviews and focus groups, and a mixed-methods co-design protocol for a digital toolbox for care leaders. Topics include adaptation during the COVID-19 pandemic, management strategies, palliative home care, nurse presenteeism and case study methodology.

name: Maren Kristine Raknes Sogstad
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Maren Kristine Raknes Sogstad studies long-term care for older adults and for children with complex needs, focusing on how services are organised, allocated and experienced, mainly in Norway. Her work combines qualitative methods (interviews, focus groups, observation), register-based and survey analyses, systematic reviews, and cross-country comparisons of care systems. Topics include service allocation and needs assessment, informal carers, care-related quality of life measured with ASCOT, intermediate care, care workforce resilience, and integrated family-centred care for children with cerebral palsy.

name: Olav Røise
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Olav Røise's research centres on trauma care and injury epidemiology, particularly traumatic brain injury, using national registry linkages, prospective cohorts, machine learning, Mendelian randomization and systematic review. Studies cover trauma registry development and triage prediction, long-term outcomes such as disability, work absence, rehabilitation pathways and opioid use after injury, and injuries from cycling, micromobility and martial arts. He also uses qualitative interviews to examine clinical decision-making and healthcare resilience in hospital transfer, pain management, home care and nursing home settings.

name: Esa Olavi Lilja
summary: Esa Olavi Lilja studies harmony in early heavy metal, looking at distorted chords, modes, harmonic function and musical texture in music from the late 1960s to the late 1980s. His work uses music-theoretical analysis of representative repertoire and clarifies terms such as tonal, modal and counterpoint as they apply to the genre. It also proposes stylistic categories to support musical style analysis.

name: Halvor Kristiansson Hosar
summary: Halvor Kristiansson Hosar studies eighteenth-century Central European music, with a focus on the composers Johann Baptist Wanhal and Carl Ditters von Dittersdorf. His work draws on archival and catalog research into monastic music collections, such as the one at Osek, and on critical editing of symphonies. It also looks at keyboard teaching traditions and at how the reforms of Joseph II affected sacred music practice.

name: Lise Karin Meling
summary: Lise Karin Meling studies women in classical music of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, with a focus on the English composer, teacher and performer Maria Hester Park. Her work combines biographical research, analysis of keyboard compositions and examination of publishing practices such as subscription publishing. It places Park's career within London's cultural life and the social expectations placed on women musicians of the period.

name: Birgitte Bauer-Nilsen
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Birgitte Bauer-Nilsen's listed work, a 2022 publication titled "Animist Pedagogies and the Endings of Worlds Rituals for the Pluriverse", suggests research at the intersection of education, animist worldviews and ritual practice. Based on the title alone, it appears to examine how teaching and learning can engage with the idea of multiple coexisting worlds and with the ending of existing ones. No abstract or methods are available, so the specific approaches and application settings cannot be described.

name: Kari Marie Manum
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Kari Marie Manum writes in the philosophy of education, with a focus on pedagogical relations, music education and the conditions of university life. Her publications use essayistic, aesthetic and vignette-based writing, together with philosophical and literary sources, to examine topics such as musicking, academic freedom, authoritarianism, degrowth, longing and human flourishing. The work applies these ideas to schooling, higher education and music teaching, including questions of power, inclusion and democracy.

name: Kristoffer Berre Alberts
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Kristoffer Berre Alberts studies how art and culture relate to smart city policy, drawing on Stavanger's strategy of building art into its smart city approach. His chapter takes a critical, manifesto-style approach, examining 'artwashing' and the role of smart ideas in artistic practice, and illustrates its argument with a musical case study by Block Ensemble. The work sits in urban studies, cultural policy and the arts, with attention to creative problem solving and urban citizenship.

name: Mari Flønes
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Mari Flønes researches choreography and dance education, focusing on how a choreographer, researcher and teacher develops practice through collaboration with school pupils and teachers. Her work uses a/r/tography, performative inquiry and diffractive analysis, drawing on agential realism and expanded ideas of choreography to examine bodily felt moments in a dance project in a Norwegian elementary school. It links theory and practice across choreography, research and teaching in primary school settings.

name: Mark William Drews
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production

name: Petter Frost Fadnes
department: Department of Jazz, Dance, Practical-Pedagogical Education and Music Production
summary: Petter Frost Fadnes studies jazz and contemporary improvised music, focusing on performance practices, hybridity and cross-cultural collaboration, including work involving Roma diaspora musicians and Norwegian, Slovakian and Czech artists. His work draws on practice-based and reflective approaches, including fieldnotes and case studies of specific ensembles and pieces. He also examines the role of art and music in urban settings, such as the place of the arts within smart city policy in Stavanger and the function of jazz venues in city music scenes.

name: Abdelrahman T. Abdelaal
summary: Abdelrahman T. Abdelaal works on chemical inhibitors that prevent mineral scale (gypsum, calcite and barite) in oilfield and industrial water systems. His recent work coats or functionalizes magnetite nanoparticles with polymers, bio-based coatings or phosphonates so the inhibitors can be recovered magnetically and reused, testing them in static and high-pressure, high-temperature dynamic experiments, with electron microscopy and spectroscopic characterization. Earlier work synthesized series of phosphonate inhibitors with varied structure and compared their calcium tolerance, thermal stability and scale inhibition performance, and one study assessed the ecotoxicity of nanoparticle inhibitors in a zebrafish embryo model.

name: Ali H. Karaly
summary: Ali H. Karaly works on polymer-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles and phosphonated polymers, mainly as recyclable, lower-discharge inhibitors of oilfield mineral scale and gas hydrates. Methods include nanoparticle synthesis and spectroscopic characterization, static and high-pressure dynamic tube-blocking tests, DFT simulations and zebrafish embryo ecotoxicity assays. Related work covers heavy metal removal from water, and biomedical and materials applications such as hemostatic sponges, wound-healing nanomaterials, antimicrobial fabrics and nanovesicle drug delivery.

name: Andrea Bagi
summary: Andrea Bagi studies microbial communities in aquatic and marine settings, using qPCR, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, fluorescence in situ hybridization and microbial source tracking. Her work covers molecular detection of oil pollution through hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria and their genes, tracing sewage contamination at a coastal outfall in Norway, and nitrifying bacteria and plankton in integrated shrimp and tilapia biofloc aquaculture. Applications include marine environmental monitoring, water quality assessment and sustainable aquaculture production.

name: Ashika Dilshani Wackwella Gamage
summary: Ashika Dilshani Wackwella Gamage studies how supercritical carbon dioxide can be used to coat and modify metal-organic framework particles, specifically ZIF-8 treated with adipic dihydrazide, for use in composite membranes. The work combines high-pressure impregnation methods with characterization by FTIR, XRD, TGA, BET and electron microscopy, and tests cellulose acetate mixed matrix membranes for hydrogen permeation. The application focus is gas separation, particularly hydrogen and carbon dioxide mixtures.

name: B. Heidari
summary: B. Heidari studies plant molecular biology in Arabidopsis, focusing on protein phosphatase 2A regulation, meiotic chromosome cohesion, trehalose-6-phosphate signalling, and responses to metal and nitrogen stress, using mutant phenotyping, gene expression, photosynthesis measurements and binding assays. The publications also cover fungal and microbial biodiversity, including global DNA metabarcoding datasets of aquatic fungi, a checklist of macrofungi in Iran, and latitudinal patterns in honey bee interaction partners identified from honey.

name: Cathrine Lillo
summary: Cathrine Lillo studies how protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) subunits and related signalling pathways, including trehalose-6-phosphate, regulate development, metabolism and stress responses in plants, mainly Arabidopsis. Her work combines mutant phenotyping, gene expression, photosynthesis and enzyme activity measurements, phosphoproteomics, protein interaction assays and microscale thermophoresis. She also examines nutrient supply, waterlogging and cultivation systems in tomato, Artemisia annua and Hypericum perforatum, including effects on nitrogen metabolism and the accumulation and root exudation of medicinal compounds.

name: Cato Brede
summary: Cato Brede works in analytical and clinical chemistry, developing liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry methods and sample preparation approaches such as salting-out assisted extraction to measure hormones, bile acids, tryptophan metabolites, hepcidin and vitamin D in human serum, fish plasma and feces. These methods are applied to clinical biomarker work in pneumonia and neuroendocrine cancer (including patient-derived organoids and metabolomics), to fish physiology and welfare in farmed Atlantic salmon, and to isolating and structurally characterizing cytotoxic plant natural products by chromatography and NMR.

name: Daniela Maria Pampanin
summary: Daniela Maria Pampanin studies how pharmaceuticals, nanomaterial waste and other emerging contaminants affect aquatic organisms, mainly early life stage zebrafish, fish cell lines and marine invertebrates. Methods include visual behaviour assays, histology, transcriptomics, in vitro cell assays and machine-learning-based digital pathology for environmental samples. She also works on seaweed, especially Palmaria palmata, covering cultivation, stress resilience, bioactivity and functional food uses, as well as encapsulation of feed ingredients for aquaculture.

name: Dugassa Nemie-Feyissa
summary: Dugassa Nemie-Feyissa studies how protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and related signalling components regulate development and stress responses in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The publications combine mutant and overexpression plant lines, gene expression, element and enzyme analyses, photosynthesis measurements and microscale thermophoresis binding assays to examine chromosome cohesion in meiosis, flowering time, nitrogen responses, photosynthetic performance and metal homeostasis. The work also includes a review of PP2A B' subunit families and covers trehalose-6-phosphate signalling and environmental stress tolerance in plants.

name: Eduardo A. Silva
summary: Eduardo A. Silva's publications cover biomaterials for tissue repair, with a focus on alginate hydrogels that release antimicrobial peptides or carry stem cell spheroids. The work combines hydrogel design and characterization with in vitro cell assays and mouse models of infected diabetic wounds and volumetric muscle loss, and also includes reviews of wound dressings for diabetic foot ulcers and of 3D culture for studying COVID-19 muscle impairment. Application areas include chronic wound care, antimicrobial-resistant infection, skeletal muscle regeneration and regenerative medicine.

name: Emiel A.M. Janssen
summary: Emiel A.M. Janssen's research combines pathology with computational methods to study breast, prostate, bladder, cervical and bowel disease. His work includes deep learning on whole-slide histopathology images for tumour segmentation, mitotic counting, Gleason grading, molecular subtyping and outcome prediction, alongside biomarker studies using ctDNA, imaging mass cytometry and digital image analysis. He also contributes to neoadjuvant treatment trials, real-world patient monitoring, biobanking protocols and health-economic evaluation of breast cancer testing.

name: Emil Anders Lindbäck
summary: Emil Anders Lindbäck works on the synthesis and biological testing of iminosugars, azasugars and related carbohydrate derivatives, including isofagomine, 1-deoxynojirimycin and arabinitol analogues. His studies use copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition to build hybrids and conjugates with coumarins, tacrine, benzotriazole, human milk oligosaccharides and fluoroquinolones. These compounds are evaluated in vitro as glycosidase and cholinesterase inhibitors, as antimicrobial agents, and against cancer cells, with docking and DFT calculations supporting the work in Alzheimer's disease, cancer and infection.

name: Emilius Adrianus Maria Janssen
summary: Emilius Adrianus Maria Janssen's research centres on diagnostic and prognostic pathology in cancer, covering breast, prostate, cervical and melanocytic tumours. His work includes blood-based tumour DNA sequencing to detect breast cancer relapse, survival analyses of histological markers in triple-negative breast cancer, and prospective screening studies for HPV-positive women using p16/Ki-67 dual staining. He also develops and validates AI and machine learning tools for digital pathology, including scanner color calibration and prostate biopsy grading, and algorithms for classifying spitzoid tumours.

name: Federico Fenaroli
summary: Federico Fenaroli studies nanoparticle-based drug delivery, with a focus on polymeric micelles, polymersomes and semiconducting polymer nanoparticles as carriers for antibiotics, host-directed drugs, anticancer agents and immune stimulants. He uses zebrafish embryo and larval infection and xenograft models, together with mouse studies, cell assays and microscopy, to evaluate toxicity, circulation, cellular uptake and therapeutic efficacy, especially for tuberculosis and Mycobacterium marinum infection. His work also includes antitubercular compound design and pharmacokinetic profiling, microfluidic micelle production, and the effect of polymer design on protein fouling.

name: Georgeio Semaan
summary: Georgeio Semaan studies the conversion of lignocellulosic and food-industry wastes such as spent coffee grounds, brewer's spent grain, crop residues and date palm waste into fuels and chemicals. The work combines laboratory pretreatment and anaerobic digestion experiments, designed with response surface methods and characterized by spectroscopy and microscopy, with process simulation and techno-economic modelling that uses sensitivity and Monte Carlo analysis. It also looks at integrating Bitcoin mining with biorefineries as an added revenue source.

name: Gopalakrishnan Kumar
summary: Gopalakrishnan Kumar's publications cover bioenergy and biorefinery processes, including anaerobic digestion of sludge and manure, microwave-assisted pyrolysis, and the fermentation and catalytic conversion of lignocellulosic biomass into ethanol, butanol, lactic acid and sustainable aviation fuel. Other work addresses emerging contaminants such as PFAS, microplastics, antibiotic resistance genes and nitrosamines, using methods including metagenomics, molecular docking, field monitoring, life cycle assessment and techno-economic analysis. Further topics include waste-derived biopolymers, microalgae wastewater treatment, fungal recycling of hygiene products, carbon capture policy and urban water circular economy governance.

name: Guido Werner Alves
summary: Guido Werner Alves studies the clinical course, prognosis and biology of Parkinson's disease and related disorders, with a focus on cognitive decline, dementia and institutionalisation. His work combines individual patient data meta-analyses of population-based cohorts, longitudinal statistical and prognostic modelling, genetic analyses, fluid biomarker assays and brain tissue proteomic and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiling. He also works on clinical rating scale validation and on cognitive outcomes in long-term survivors of brain metastases.

name: Hanne Røland Hagland
summary: Hanne Røland Hagland works on cancer biology and biomaterials, combining laboratory models with clinical cohort data. Her publications cover patient-derived organoids and 2D/3D cell cultures for drug testing in pancreatic and colorectal cancer, preclinical testing of anti-CD47 fusion proteins in lymphoma and leukemia, and registry-based analyses of outcomes after pancreatic surgery. She also studies the biocompatibility and toxicity of graphene materials and 3D-printed bone scaffolds using cell assays, zebrafish larvae and mechanical testing.

name: Ilke Pala Øzkøk
summary: Ilke Pala Øzkøk studies biological wastewater treatment, focusing on activated sludge and hybrid biofilm (MBBR) systems for removing nutrients and micropollutants such as anti-inflammatory drugs and antibiotics. Her work combines respirometry, kinetic and plant-wide process modelling, and DNA sequencing of microbial communities, and also covers antibiotic resistance and disinfectant effects in treatment plants. She additionally investigates producing polyhydroxyalkanoate biopolymers from saline and organic-acid-rich waste streams using mixed microbial cultures.

name: Janronel Pomicpic
summary: Janronel Pomicpic studies kinetic hydrate inhibitors, which are chemicals that stop gas hydrates from blocking oil and gas production flow lines. The work combines polymer synthesis (including poly(2-amino-2-oxazoline)s, dipeptoids, block and statistical copolymers, and maleic-based copolymers) with high-pressure rocking cell tests, and examines synergists such as amine oxides, phosphine oxides and glycol ethers. Related work covers how molecular structure affects performance, mixed clathrate hydrate formation, and combining hydrate inhibition with corrosion and scale control.

name: Jason T. Magnuson
summary: Jason T. Magnuson studies how environmental contaminants affect the health of early life stage fish, mainly zebrafish, with additional work on human exposure to PFAS and artificial sweeteners. The work covers pesticides, pharmaceuticals, PCBs, PFAS, preservatives, antioxidants and plastic-product leachates, using transcriptomics, metabolomics, mass spectrometry, behavioural and visual function assays, histology and pathway-inhibitor experiments to probe immune, neurological, visual and cardiac effects. It also includes machine learning toxicity prediction, benchmark dose modelling for safety thresholds, meta-analysis and mother–infant cohort analysis, and commentary on using omics in ecological risk assessment and regulation.

name: Jeff Tomiak
summary: Jeff Tomiak studies the human gut microbiome, with a focus on intestinal protists such as Blastocystis and Dientamoeba fragilis and on faecal microbiota transplantation. The work includes a clinical case report on clearing multidrug-resistant bacteria with FMT capsules and a population study using 16S and 18S rDNA sequencing and machine learning to link Blastocystis carriage to bacterial and eukaryotic gut communities. It also includes commentary on Blastocystis as a possible marker of gut health and on parasite transmission through FMT.

name: Jens Vikse
summary: Jens Vikse works in clinical rheumatology, with a focus on IgG4-related disease and on interstitial lung disease linked to connective tissue disorders. His work uses multicenter cohort studies, guideline development with GRADE methodology, Delphi consensus exercises, meta-analysis and registry analysis, and it covers rituximab and glucocorticoid treatment, diagnostic criteria across disease phenotypes, and adherence to guidelines. He has also contributed to guideline methodology for the use of expert opinion, and to studies of COVID-19 treatment and of ECMO in children with immunodeficiency.

name: Jodi Maple Grødem
summary: Jodi Maple Grødem studies Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, focusing on disease progression, prognosis and biomarkers. Her work uses pooled analyses of population-based incidence cohorts, genetic association and survival analyses, and fluid biomarker assays (SIMOA, seed amplification, cell-free DNA, enzyme activity) alongside scale validation and risk-prediction modelling. The applications include diagnosis, dementia and institutionalisation risk prediction, clinical trial design and patient information.

name: Johannes Lange
summary: Johannes Lange studies fluid and genetic biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of Parkinson's disease and related disorders such as dementia with Lewy bodies and Alzheimer's disease. The work analyses cerebrospinal fluid and serum from population-based cohorts like ParkWest, using seed amplification assays, SIMOA, proximity extension proteomics, cell-free DNA sequencing and enzyme activity measures, with mixed-effects and survival models relating markers to cognitive and motor decline. It also includes systematic reviews, an individual patient data meta-analysis of disease prognosis, multi-laboratory assay comparisons, and cell-based retinal neuroprotection research.

name: John Senith Ravishan Fernando
summary: John Senith Ravishan Fernando studies porous adsorbent materials for CO2 capture and separation, including zirconium and cerium metal-organic frameworks and pillar[5]arene-based supramolecular organic frameworks. The work combines framework synthesis and functionalization, structural characterization, and gas and water vapour adsorption tests covering selectivity, cyclability and stability under humid conditions. It also includes shaping bio-based MOFs into beads, as a step toward flue gas separation at larger scale.

name: Kjetil Bårdsen
summary: Kjetil Bårdsen studies the biological basis of fatigue in chronic inflammatory and neurological diseases, including Parkinson's disease, Crohn's disease and psoriasis. The work combines patient-reported fatigue scales with molecular measurements such as cerebrospinal fluid proteomics, plasma biomarkers and blood gene expression (RNA sequencing and RT-qPCR), analysed with regression and principal component analysis. It focuses on innate immune and cellular stress pathways, including HMGB1, interleukin-1 signalling and heat-shock proteins.

name: Klevia Dishnica
summary: Klevia Dishnica works across computational and laboratory life sciences, with a focus on infectious disease and molecular biology. Her publications use molecular dynamics simulations, interaction-based drug repositioning screens, genomic sequencing and variant analysis, mass spectrometry proteomics, and clinical diagnostic evaluation to study SARS-CoV-2, the parasite Strongyloides stercoralis, and chemokine receptor signalling. She has also applied cell-based assays and transcriptomics to test how seaweed extracts affect intestinal epithelial cells, relevant to functional foods.

name: Krista Michelle Kaster
summary: Krista Michelle Kaster studies antibiotic resistance and microbial communities in wastewater treatment, using qPCR, 16S rRNA and high-throughput sequencing, minimum inhibitory concentration tests, and laboratory-scale reactors. Her work covers how low antibiotic levels, disinfectants and antiseptics, and seasonal and source differences affect the spread of resistance genes in treatment plants and receiving waters, including field monitoring at Norwegian plants. She has also investigated low-temperature anaerobic granule reactors for treating municipal wastewater and producing methane.

name: Kåre Bredeli Jørgensen
summary: Kåre Bredeli Jørgensen works in synthetic organic and materials chemistry, preparing pillararene macrocycles and their quinone derivatives, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and their oxidized metabolites, nanographenes and azasugar compounds. Methods include photochemical cyclization, chemical and flow-electrochemical oxidation, post-synthetic modification of metal-organic frameworks, gas sorption, spectroscopy and ab initio calculations. Applications covered include CO2 capture, host-guest chemistry, biomass fractionation, glycosidase inhibition and toxicity studies of crude-oil PAHs in fish embryos.

name: Lutz Andreas Eichacker
summary: Lutz Andreas Eichacker's publications span plant molecular physiology, structural biology and nanomedicine. They include work on how a trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase affects flowering time, nitrogen responses and photosynthesis in Arabidopsis mutants and overexpressing lines, and an X-ray free-electron laser study that recorded a diffraction pattern from a single GroEL protein. They also include a comparison of oxidized and PEGylated graphene as carriers for the cancer drug phenformin, tested in human cells and zebrafish larvae.

name: Magne O. Sydnes
summary: Magne O. Sydnes works in synthetic and medicinal chemistry, preparing azasugars such as isofagomine derivatives, indoloquinoline alkaloids, antibiotic conjugates and peptide or polymer conjugates, and testing them for enzyme inhibition, antimicrobial, anticancer and neuroprotective activity. His work also covers the environmental fate of pharmaceuticals, including photodegradable antibiotics studied by NMR and mass spectrometry, wastewater risk modelling and effects on fish gene expression. Collaborative publications add lipid metabolism and fatty acid oxidation studies in rodents and the formulation of hydrogels for drug release.

name: Malcolm A. Kelland
summary: Malcolm A. Kelland's publications address flow assurance and chemical treatment in oil and gas production, focusing on mineral scale inhibition and kinetic hydrate inhibitors. The work includes synthesising phosphonate, polymer-coated and magnetic nanoparticle inhibitors that can be recovered and reused, and evaluating them in static, high-pressure dynamic and rocking cell tests. Related studies cover barite scale dissolvers, polymer structure and synergists for hydrate inhibition, and environmental assessment through zebrafish embryo toxicity and biodegradation testing of produced water.

name: Mari Mæland Nilsen
summary: Mari Mæland Nilsen works on molecular approaches to fatigue in chronic disease and on DNA-based detection in aquaculture. Her publications use proteomics of cerebrospinal fluid in Parkinson's disease and RNA sequencing with RT-qPCR of heat-shock protein genes in psoriasis, and she also developed a qPCR assay to detect and quantify salmon lice from seawater environmental DNA samples near fish farms.

name: Mark van der Giezen
summary: Mark van der Giezen studies gut and other human- and animal-associated microbial communities, with a particular focus on intestinal protists such as Blastocystis, Entamoeba and Balantioides coli. His work combines 16S/ITS sequencing, metabarcoding, comparative genomics, phylogenetics, crystallography and genetic tool development, and is applied in clinical trials and cohort studies of gut, oral and skin microbiomes, nutrition, and disease. He also contributes to digital health and AI projects for early detection and monitoring of Alzheimer's disease, cancer-related fatigue and inflammatory bowel disease.

name: Melinda Lillesand
summary: Melinda Lillesand works on digital pathology and prognostic biomarkers in cancer, combining deep learning on whole-slide images with immunohistochemistry, targeted sequencing, RNA sequencing and imaging mass cytometry. Her publications cover tumour segmentation and mitotic figure counting validated across many cancer types, and risk stratification and treatment response in bladder cancer, with further work on endometrial hyperplasia and cervical precancer. The studies mostly use large retrospective patient cohorts with survival analysis to test whether markers predict recurrence, progression or therapy outcome.

name: Nina Egeland
summary: Nina Egeland's publications span nursing education and breast cancer research. One paper compares national legislation on public health nurse education and services across the Nordic countries to identify ways the programmes could collaborate. Another is a protocol for a long-term observational biobank study in Western Norway that follows women with early-stage breast cancer using repeated blood and urine samples and patient-reported questionnaires to look for biomarkers of relapse and to study fatigue and quality of life.

name: Oddmund Nordgård
summary: Oddmund Nordgård studies liquid biopsy biomarkers in breast and pancreatic cancer, including circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, disseminated tumor cells and extracellular vesicle DNA. The work uses targeted sequencing, PCR-based assays, DNA methylation and fragmentomics with machine learning, and survival modelling, and includes development of an error-corrected sequencing method. Applications include earlier detection of relapse or progression, prediction of clinical outcome, treatment monitoring including immunotherapy, and prospective biobanking of patients with early breast cancer.

name: Pierre Edouard Liboureau
summary: Pierre Edouard Liboureau studies seaweeds, covering the physiology, cultivation and bioactive potential of red and brown algae such as Palmaria palmata, Alaria esculenta and Laminaria pallida. The work combines growth and photosynthesis measurements, stress and thermal-history experiments, proteomics, transcriptomics and cell-based assays to examine climate resilience, antioxidant properties and gut-health effects, with applications in sustainable aquaculture and functional foods. He also works in environmental toxicology, using machine-learning histology on fish livers and modelling and bioassays to assess pharmaceutical contaminants in wastewater effluent.

name: Sachin Maruti Chavan
summary: Sachin Maruti Chavan works on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), especially zirconium- and cerium-based materials, and their use in CO2 capture, CO2 hydrogenation to methanol and metal-ion removal from water. The publications cover MOF synthesis, post-synthetic functionalization, MOF-derived Cu/ZnO catalysts, and in situ Raman, X-ray diffraction and X-ray absorption monitoring of MOF formation. Related work covers heterogeneous catalysts for ethylene-to-propylene conversion, single-atom electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction, greenhouse climate-yield modelling and a measurement technique for residual oil films in displacement flows.

name: Solveig Auranaune Markussen
summary: Solveig Auranaune Markussen works on glycosidase inhibitors, focusing on iminosugars and isoiminosugars, which are sugar-mimicking compounds relevant to drug discovery. Her review of in vitro enzyme assay data examines how adding substituents at the 1- and 5a-positions of polyhydroxylated piperidine isoiminosugars changes inhibitory activity and specificity compared with the parent compounds. It also compares common iminosugars with isoiminosugars to show how moving the ring nitrogen to the anomeric position alters inhibition.

name: Umay Kiraz
summary: Umay Kiraz works in computational and digital pathology, building deep learning models, including weakly supervised and multiple-instance learning approaches, to analyze whole-slide images for breast and bladder cancer. Her work covers molecular subtype prediction, prognosis and treatment response, mitosis detection, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte assessment, and artifact detection with uncertainty estimation for quality control. She also studies prognostic and predictive biomarkers in population-based triple-negative and luminal breast cancer cohorts, and has contributed to genomic sequencing and tissue biomechanics studies.

name: Venkatesh Bollabathini
summary: Venkatesh Bollabathini works on the synthesis and characterization of pillararene macrocycles, including pillar[5]arene and pillar[5]/[6]quinone derivatives. His publications combine synthetic chemistry, NMR and infrared spectroscopy and ab initio calculations to study host-guest complexes and noncovalent interactions. He also applies hydroxy-pillararene-based supramolecular organic frameworks to selective CO2 capture and separation, including testing under humid conditions.

name: Yohannes Seyoum
summary: Yohannes Seyoum studies the gut and skin microbiota and how it relates to nutrition, diet and disease, mainly using 16S rRNA and ITS sequencing alongside PCR, metabolomics and mouse models. The publications cover human clinical and randomized trials (inflammatory bowel disease, cognitive decline, school-based micronutrient fortification), intestinal parasites such as Balantioides coli and Blastocystis, and fermented cereal foods in Africa and Europe. Further work includes reviews and modelling of anemia and vitamin A supplementation in West and sub-Saharan Africa, and a protocol using wearables and real-world data to monitor cancer-related fatigue.

name: Ahmad Opeyemi Zubair
summary: Ahmad Opeyemi Zubair studies power distribution networks, focusing on optimal power flow and loss analysis. His work tests how well AI-based surrogate models solve optimal power flow as solar and wind distributed energy resources increase, and uses forward/backward sweep power flow in MATLAB to quantify technical losses and voltage problems on a real Nigerian 11 kV radial feeder. The applications are distribution network planning, loss reduction and reliable operation of grids with high renewable penetration.

name: Ali Gohar
summary: Ali Gohar studies resource allocation in virtualized 5G and smart city networks, focusing on network slicing, multi-access edge computing and virtual network embedding. The work formulates these problems as optimization tasks and solves them with deep reinforcement learning, including policy gradient methods, comparing results against benchmark and state-of-the-art algorithms. Applications include minimizing costs for slice brokers that buy resources from infrastructure providers and enforcing isolation between virtual networks sharing physical infrastructure.

name: Alvaro Fernandez Quilez
summary: Alvaro Fernandez Quilez develops deep learning methods for medical image analysis, mainly structural MRI of the brain and prostate, along with some work on EEG and cardiac imaging. The publications cover Alzheimer's disease risk prediction and prostate cancer detection and segmentation, using techniques such as ensemble models, normative modelling, self-supervised and multimodal learning, and conformal prediction for uncertainty. Much of the work also examines how well the models would hold up in clinical use, including calibration, fairness across gender groups, variable acquisition protocols and errors that arise when system components are combined.

name: Annisa Sarah
summary: Annisa Sarah researches resource allocation, service migration and routing in 5G and beyond networks that use Multi-access Edge Computing. Her work formulates optimization problems and solves them with exact solvers, scoring-based heuristics, Q-routing and deep reinforcement learning, balancing latency, availability, privacy and cost. Application areas include low-latency mobile services, network slicing with slice brokers, and AI-based orchestration for smart cities.

name: Antorweep Chakravorty
summary: Antorweep Chakravorty works on decentralized and privacy-preserving systems, with publications on blockchain-based social media tools and on secure peer-to-peer energy trading. His work includes building a decentralized app for citizen crowd journalism with a token-based content marketplace, and designing an anonymous access control protocol that hides user identities in electricity trading. He also appears as author of several preface pieces for proceedings or volumes.

name: Arezo Shakeri
summary: Arezo Shakeri studies how language and speech can be used to detect Alzheimer's disease, dementia and mild cognitive impairment at an early stage. Her work applies natural language processing, classical machine learning, transformer models and statistical tests (ANOVA) to speech transcripts and conversations, with attention to multilingual and low-resource languages such as Norwegian and Chinese. She has also built unified and translated datasets and carried out a systematic review of NLP methods and data in Alzheimer's research.

name: Azadeh Jirdehi
summary: Azadeh Jirdehi works on modelling, system identification and control of unmanned aerial vehicle platforms, using the Quanser 3DoF Hover as a test system. Her publications build a nonlinear model that includes friction and gravity, estimate its parameters through lab experiments and genetic algorithm optimisation, and then test whether the more detailed model improves trajectory tracking. The control work combines feedforward control with linear parameter-varying error feedback designed through linear matrix inequalities, and is validated in real-time experiments.

name: Boyu Cui
summary: Boyu Cui works on automated analysis of permanent downhole gauge data for well and reservoir monitoring, developing methods to identify pressure transients and integrating them into time-lapse pressure transient analysis workflows. These methods have been tested on North Sea injection wells and on geothermal wells in Indonesia, and the work is complemented by simulation studies. Related work applies machine learning to subsurface and industrial problems, including federated learning for drilling rate-of-penetration prediction, a controllable autoencoder for parameter analysis, and a federated language-model system for tacit knowledge in oil and gas.

name: Casper Cappelen
summary: Casper Cappelen works on deep learning for medical image analysis, focusing on automatic segmentation of the myocardium in late gadolinium enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance images. The publication compares two U-Net variants, one with residual connections and one multiresolution, and tests how different pixel value scaling strategies in preprocessing affect performance when models are applied to a different dataset. The work is relevant to cardiac MRI and semi-automated segmentation workflows, with evaluation based on Jaccard scores.

name: Chunming Rong
summary: Chunming Rong's research covers distributed and privacy-preserving machine learning, including federated learning with heterogeneous or quantized clients, online and class-incremental learning, and deep reinforcement learning for UAV-assisted edge computing and network service placement. It also covers blockchain and smart contract work such as vulnerability detection, consent management and incentive mechanisms for threat intelligence markets. Applications include oil and gas well monitoring and drilling data, and AI video analysis of newborn resuscitation in a hospital pilot.

name: Damiano Rotondo
summary: Damiano Rotondo works on control theory for dynamic systems, with emphasis on fault estimation and fault-tolerant control, sampled-data systems, linear parameter-varying systems, model predictive control and iterative learning control. His methods combine linear matrix inequality design, data-driven and identification-based modelling, observers and genetic-algorithm optimisation, tested in simulation and on laboratory platforms such as tank systems, a Quanser Aero, a 3DoF Hover and a DC motor-propeller. Application examples also include underwater vehicle design and anaesthesia regulation, alongside work on control education and outreach.

name: Daniel Osmundsen Dirdal

position.nb: Stipendiat i datateknologi : Verifikasjon av distribuerte systemer

summary: Daniel Osmundsen Dirdal works on formal modeling and verification of concurrent and distributed systems. His publications write a TLA+ specification of the Beefy light-client protocol used in Polkadot and check it with the TLC and Apalache model checkers, and also build a Petri net simulation platform in GPenSIM for comparing multiprocessor scheduling algorithms. The work applies to blockchain protocol assurance and to performance evaluation of parallel computing systems.

name: Didrik Efjestad Fjereide
summary: Didrik Efjestad Fjereide works on engineering education, specifically the use of games to teach automatic control. His publication adapts the inductive logic board game Zendo into a classroom game in which students guess hidden rules about system properties such as linearity, time variation and the number of inputs and outputs. The work covers how the game was implemented and the feedback from students who played it in a basic control course at the University of Stavanger.

name: Eivind Sandve Haus
summary: Eivind Sandve Haus studies mathematical modelling of biomolecular regulatory systems, focusing on structural identifiability of negative-feedback controller motifs such as basic and antithetic motifs. The work systematically analyzes over a hundred motif structures under different combinations of concentration and flow measurements, and proposes ways to include flow measurements as model outputs. The findings show how motif complexity and measurement choice determine whether model parameters can be uniquely determined, which is relevant to building and evaluating models of biological systems.

name: Enrico Guerriero
summary: Enrico Guerriero works on automated recognition of fine-grained activities in video, with a focus on newborn resuscitation. His work compares locally run vision-language models, paired with large language models, against a supervised TimeSformer vision transformer baseline on simulated resuscitation recordings. The methods include zero-shot prompting and fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation, applied to support clinical documentation and quality improvement.

name: Erlend Tøssebro
summary: Erlend Tøssebro works on computer vision and deep learning for healthcare, with a focus on recognizing activities in video of neonatal resuscitation. His work combines thermal and visible light video, two-stream fusion models and MoViNet-based activity recognition to detect time of birth and key resuscitation actions such as ventilation, stimulation and suction. He also builds web dashboards that let clinicians view and compare automated and manual timelines, tested in a single-hospital pilot for debriefing and quality improvement.

name: Ferhat Özgur Catak
summary: Ferhat Özgur Catak works on trustworthy and secure machine learning, including federated learning, uncertainty quantification for large language and vision-language models, and adversarial robustness. His publications apply deep learning and transformer models to wireless communications such as spectrum sensing, channel estimation and modulation classification, and to healthcare, energy forecasting and document classification. He also writes on quantum machine learning theory, quantum key distribution for secure model training, and generative AI in smart grids.

name: Florenc Demrozi
summary: Florenc Demrozi works on machine learning for wearable and ambient sensing, covering human activity recognition, fall detection (including pre-impact detection with airbag jackets and event-camera vision) and freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease. His methods include lightweight deep learning models for microcontrollers and edge devices, few-shot and zero-shot learning, automatic labelling, federated and continual learning, and indoor localization without offline mapping. He also contributes public sensor datasets and benchmarking studies, plus reviews of multimodal AI in healthcare, for applications in healthcare monitoring, workplace safety and smart environments.

name: Gabriel Emerson Iturra Bocaz
summary: Gabriel Emerson Iturra Bocaz works on information retrieval and natural language processing, with a focus on retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop question answering, including metacognitive and multi-agent designs and a reproducibility study. He also contributes to shared-task evaluation, such as the LongEval lab on longitudinal retrieval performance and the CheckThat! numerical fact-checking task, and has studied how relevance judgment depth affects BERT-based reranking. Further work covers a domain-specific RAG system for NASA aerospace documents, tested with automated metrics and user studies, and an open-source Python library for incremental word embeddings on text streams.

name: Gianfranco Nencioni
summary: Gianfranco Nencioni studies resource management, service placement and migration, and security and dependability in 5G and beyond networks that use multi-access edge computing and network slicing. His work combines optimization, multi-objective heuristics, graph-based path computation, reinforcement learning, and dependability and security modeling, tested through simulation and Kubernetes-based testbeds. Application areas include low-latency and mission-critical services, vehicular communication, smart cities, and the economics of slice brokers.

name: Hein Meling
summary: Hein Meling works on distributed systems and blockchain technology, with a focus on Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, including role assignment, vote aggregation, incentive design, and implementation and testing frameworks for protocols such as HotStuff. His work also covers formal specification and model checking in TLA+, authenticated data structures for time-travel queries, privacy-preserving digital credentials using zero-knowledge proofs, and decentralized storage maintenance. He also contributes reproducibility reviews of database and data-management research papers.

name: Ivica Kostric
summary: Ivica Kostric studies conversational recommender systems and conversational search, covering evaluation methodology, user modeling and system building. The publications include reproducibility studies of benchmark methods, new datasets and tasks for estimating user domain knowledge, controlled user experiments on conversational style, and neural query rewriting for passage retrieval. The work also covers research platforms and tools such as a movie recommender, a conference assistant chatbot and robot, and a personal knowledge graph management API.

name: Jayachander Surbiryala
summary: Jayachander Surbiryala works on decentralized cloud marketplaces, focusing on how service level agreements can be made trustworthy among multiple cloud providers. The publication presents a framework that combines auction-based service selection, a committee of witnesses and smart contract orchestration, built as a prototype application on the Ethereum blockchain. It is evaluated experimentally for latency and cost, with relevance to cloud application development and operations.

name: John Håkon Husøy
summary: John Håkon Husøy works on adaptive digital signal processing, with a focus on subband adaptive filtering and its relationship to the normalized least mean square algorithm. His 2022 work proposes a very simple two-band filter bank for the normalized subband adaptive filter, supported by theoretical arguments and simulation studies of convergence performance against computational cost. The research is relevant to system identification and other applications where efficient adaptive filters are needed.

name: Jorge García-Torres
summary: Jorge García-Torres works on AI-based video analysis for newborn care, using deep learning on thermal and visible light recordings to detect the time of birth and recognise resuscitation activities such as ventilation, stimulation and suction. His work includes thermal image normalisation, two-stream fusion models, activity recognition networks, a clinician-facing timeline dashboard and the design of consent-based video data collection at Stavanger University Hospital. The applications are privacy-preserving documentation, debriefing and quality improvement in delivery rooms and resuscitation settings.

name: Jungwon Seo
summary: Jungwon Seo works on federated learning, developing aggregation and optimization methods that address client drift, partial participation, mixed-precision quantization and secure aggregation (including quantum key distribution and neural homomorphic encryption), supported by theoretical analysis and benchmark experiments. The work also covers large language models, including uncertainty quantification with embedding geometry, text-style transfer for customer support, and code deployment in federated systems, as well as robustness of AI in 6G and safety-critical settings. Application areas include wireless physical-layer tasks, oil and gas knowledge management and drilling prediction, industrial control, and blockchain-based carbon credit tracking.

name: K. Thorsen
summary: K. Thorsen works on modelling, identification and control of dynamical systems, including a Quanser 3DoF Hover platform, a DC motor-propeller with unknown input delay, and biomolecular feedback circuits. The methods include genetic-algorithm parameter fitting, switched and linear parameter-varying observers and controllers designed with linear matrix inequalities, and structural identifiability analysis, with validation in real-time experiments. Related work applies control theory to synthetic biology in yeast copper regulation and examines how distributed energy resources affect the feasibility of AI-based optimal power flow surrogates in distribution networks.

name: Karl Skretting
summary: Karl Skretting works on sparse representation and signal processing, developing online dictionary learning methods and sparse approximation techniques. His publications cover a kernel-based recursive least squares algorithm for updating dictionaries as data arrive, tested on classification tasks across four datasets, and a block-based sparse coding method that separates the frequency content of nonlinear signals using chirp-like atoms and a modified orthogonal matching pursuit.

name: Kathinka Dæhli Kurz
summary: Kathinka Dæhli Kurz works in clinical and AI-based radiology, with a focus on acute stroke imaging and care, and also on breast, brain tumour, cardiac and dementia imaging. Her studies combine deep learning methods (ensemble models, 4D CNNs, GANs, few-shot and segmentation networks) with retrospective and registry-based clinical studies, health service surveys and simulation training. Applications include stroke segmentation and treatment selection, access to thrombectomy, breast MRI and mammography screening, CT contrast dosing and Alzheimer's detection from MRI.

name: Ketil Oppedal
summary: Ketil Oppedal studies neurodegeneration in dementia, mainly dementia with Lewy bodies, using structural MRI, regional brain volume and cortical thickness measures, imaging transcriptomics, and clustering to examine atrophy patterns, sex differences, co-pathologies and patient subtypes. He also develops deep learning methods for medical image analysis, including dementia classification, fairness analysis, data augmentation, and prostate cancer lesion detection on MRI, and has contributed to clinical studies on early markers of cognitive decline, malnutrition in dementia, and an anthocyanin supplementation trial. Other work includes X-ray calibration for hip replacement planning.

name: Kjersti Engan
summary: Kjersti Engan works on deep learning and computer vision for medical data, with two main strands: computational pathology and neonatal care. In pathology she builds weakly supervised and multiple instance learning models for whole-slide images, artifact detection with uncertainty estimates, and spatial immune profiling for bladder cancer and inflammatory bowel disease. In neonatal care she develops thermal and visible-light video systems that detect time of birth and recognise resuscitation activities, supported by clinical observational studies, consent-based data collection with blockchain, and work on generative imaging and multimodal healthcare AI.

name: Krisztian Balog
summary: Krisztian Balog studies how people interact with search, recommender and conversational systems, with a strong focus on user simulation, benchmark datasets and evaluation methods for these systems. His work covers conversational recommender systems, retrieval-augmented generation (grounding, source attribution and user trust), and the use of large language models as rankers and judges. He combines dataset and toolkit creation, reproducibility studies, crowdsourced benchmarking and controlled user studies, including applications in scientific literature recommendation.

name: Leander Nikolaus Jehl
summary: Leander Nikolaus Jehl works on distributed systems and blockchain technology, with a focus on Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, including role assignment, scalability techniques, vote aggregation and protocol implementation frameworks. His work also covers trusted execution environments for edge and cloud deployments, formal verification with TLA+ and model checking, incentive fairness in decentralized storage networks, and decentralized and privacy-preserving identity and credential systems. Methods include system design and prototyping, simulation, experimental evaluation, formal specification and survey analysis, applied to areas such as railway data recording, edge machine learning inference and light clients.

name: Mahdieh Khanmohammadi
summary: Mahdieh Khanmohammadi works on medical image analysis for acute ischemic stroke, using computed tomography perfusion (CTP) scans. Her work applies deep learning, including 4D convolutional networks, few-shot and self-supervised segmentation, and generative adversarial networks, alongside classical machine learning compared with thresholding, to delineate core and penumbra tissue and to create synthetic 4D perfusion data. The applications are stroke diagnosis, treatment planning, clinical training and data augmentation for decision-support tools.

name: Mariam Arustashvili
summary: Mariam Arustashvili works on recommender systems for scientific literature, focusing on user interest profiles written in natural language. Her work builds a synthetic test dataset from authors' publication histories and uses it to compare sparse retrieval, dense retrieval and large language model rerankers. The research centers on evaluation resources and benchmarking for transparent, user-controllable scholarly recommendation.

name: Martin Gilje Jaatun
summary: Martin Gilje Jaatun studies cybersecurity across software development, critical infrastructure and emerging technologies, using multi-case and interview studies, surveys, system design and prototype building. His work covers security risks of generative AI in software organisations, DevSecOps automation, software bills of materials, incident response capacity, and cyber-physical security of water networks. He also develops blockchain-based approaches to decentralised identity, access control, digital object management and privacy-friendly social networks, and examines privacy and security flaws in social service robots and cloud infrastructure-as-code.

name: Matteo Iervasi
summary: Matteo Iervasi works on sensor-based human activity recognition, including a multi-sensor method that combines inertial sensors on everyday objects with Bluetooth beacon signal strength to generate training labels automatically, reducing the need for manual annotation. The approach is checked against video-based ground truth and tested by training a deep learning model on Wi-Fi channel state information data. He has also carried out a systematic review of wearable cueing technologies for Parkinson's disease, examining auditory, visual, haptic and multimodal cueing and their effects on motor symptoms.

name: Matthias Anton Schedel
summary: Matthias Anton Schedel works on modeling and simulation of automated guided vehicle (AGV) systems in manufacturing, using modular Petri nets implemented in the GPenSIM simulator on MATLAB. The publication studies how AGV battery discharge rates, fleet size and the number and placement of charging stations affect output in a toy car production line. The approach aims to give practitioners an accessible, extensible model for testing AGV operating scenarios without advanced mathematics.

name: Merkebu Zenebe Degefa
summary: Merkebu Zenebe Degefa works on the operation and control of power distribution networks with high shares of distributed energy resources and local energy communities. His publications cover microgrid synchronization and interconnection controllers, distributed and AI-based voltage control and optimal power flow, TSO-DSO data exchange, flexibility modelling for grid planning, and wide-area oscillation monitoring. Methods include simulation, optimisation (such as ADMM), scenario frameworks, and real-time and power-hardware-in-the-loop laboratory testing.

name: Mina Farmanbar
summary: Mina Farmanbar works on machine learning and natural language processing for health, especially detecting Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment from speech and conversation transcripts in several languages, including low-resource ones such as Norwegian. Her work also covers deep learning for image segmentation in remote sensing (LiDAR and aerial imagery) and cardiac MRI, machine learning prediction of fatigue life in structural steels, and reviews of multimodal AI and online learning on streaming data. Methods include transformer models, classical classifiers, statistical feature analysis, U-Net architectures, genetic algorithm optimization and systematic reviews.

name: Morten Mossige
summary: Morten Mossige works on software testing and verification for industrial robotic systems, in close collaboration with ABB Robotics. His publications apply constraint programming to automate test case generation and test execution scheduling across robots and test machines, and use model checking and hardware/software co-verification to assess the safety of robot control software. The work centres on cyber-physical systems and reports on transferring these methods into industrial practice.

name: Morteza Esmaeili
summary: Morteza Esmaeili works on magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy, with a focus on brain tumours such as glioma and glioblastoma, and on cardiac metabolism. His work applies deep learning to tumour segmentation, molecular subtype classification, spectroscopic data analysis and image super-resolution. It also uses image registration and diffusion tensor imaging to measure tumour growth along white matter, and includes reviews of MR methods for cancer characterisation, cardiac metabolism and exercise in heart failure rehabilitation.

name: Naeem Khademi
summary: Naeem Khademi studies networked systems, covering vehicle positioning in road tunnels and Internet transport protocols over satellite links. His work uses modeling of inertial sensors, simulated driving routes through Norwegian tunnels, and experiments on an emulated testbed to assess how well systems meet performance needs. Application areas include cooperative intelligent transport systems, autonomous vehicles and satellite broadband for 5G/6G networks.

name: Nan Zhang
summary: Nan Zhang works on petroleum and subsurface engineering, covering CO2 storage and enhanced oil recovery in tight and shale reservoirs, well monitoring, and drilling automation. The work combines laboratory core-flooding experiments with NMR and visualization, reservoir simulation, machine-learning surrogate models (physics-informed networks, GANs, self-attention, federated learning) and automated pressure transient analysis of permanent gauge data. It also covers downhole sensing and control, including MEMS accelerometer calibration, attitude data compression on FPGA, and rotary steerable system control tested by hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

name: Nejm Saadallah
summary: Nejm Saadallah works on the formal modeling and verification of blockchain protocols, focusing on justification layers that let resource-constrained light clients verify block finalization. The work specifies the Beefy protocol used in the Polkadot ecosystem in TLA+ and checks safety, liveness and an inductive invariant with the TLC and Apalache model checkers. It also compares the formal specification against Polkadot's informal specification and implementation, identifying a deadlock in the informal specification.

name: Peter Røysland Aarnes
summary: Peter Røysland Aarnes works on automated fact-checking, focusing on how large language models verify numerical claims and detect claims worth checking. His work uses counterfactual explanations, adversarial training, fine-tuning of transformer models, data augmentation and cross-language transfer, tested on benchmark datasets and shared-task evaluations. Application areas include countering misinformation in political debates and social media in English, Dutch and Arabic.

name: Petra Galuscakova
summary: Petra Galuscakova works on information retrieval, with a focus on longitudinal evaluation of how search systems hold up as documents, queries and relevance judgments change over time, including organising the LongEval shared-task labs at CLEF. Her work also covers retrieval-augmented generation (a reproducibility study and a NASA aerospace documentation system with user evaluation), neural reranking, fact-checking and claim detection with transformer models, and interfaces for spoken content and personal knowledge graphs. Methods include benchmark and shared-task design, reproducibility experiments, model fine-tuning and user studies.

name: Reggie Davidrajuh
summary: Reggie Davidrajuh works on Petri net theory and on GPenSIM, a MATLAB-based simulator for modeling, analyzing and controlling discrete event systems. His publications cover modular and extended Petri nets, supervisory control, delayed transitions, structural analysis of job completion times, and comparison of Petri net epidemic models against differential equation models. He applies these methods to simulations of manufacturing and automated guided vehicles, warehouse robots, traffic, queuing systems, retail checkout, multiprocessor scheduling and a strategy video game.

name: S. Ørn
summary: S. Ørn studies cardiovascular disease and sports cardiology, including how prolonged high-intensity exercise affects the heart through troponin release, echocardiographic strain and myocardial work, and autonomic responses in athletes with and without coronary artery disease or calcification. Other work uses national registry data to follow heart failure treatment patterns and outcomes, including the prognostic value of walk-test changes, and applies cardiac MRI, machine learning and deep learning segmentation to myocardial injury after infarction. Further publications cover statin effects on a biomarker after heart attack and case-level interventional cardiology.

name: Shaima Ahmad Freja
summary: Shaima Ahmad Freja works on applying machine learning and natural language processing to health-related language data, with a focus on spotting early signs of dementia in transcribed speech. Her work compares classical classifiers with transfer learning using BERT-based models on DementiaBank datasets, evaluating them through cross-validation. The application area is early, language-based screening for neurodegenerative disease.

name: Syed Tahir Hussain Rizvi
summary: Syed Tahir Hussain Rizvi works on applied machine learning and deep learning, with studies spanning time series forecasting, video-based action and crowd behavior recognition, and missing-data imputation. He also applies convolutional, Transformer and ensemble models to medical imaging (brain tumor, prostate cancer, skin cancer, COVID-19), newborn resuscitation video analysis, and sensor-glove sign language recognition. Other work covers social media sentiment analysis after disasters, comparisons of IPv6 routing protocols in simulated networks, and fuzzy control algorithms for vehicle motion simulators.

name: T. Wiktorski
summary: T. Wiktorski works on applied machine learning and data science, with a main focus on the oil and gas drilling domain. This includes large language models for question answering and ontology mapping, and deep learning for rate of penetration prediction using transfer learning, continual learning and quantile regression. The publications also cover machine learning and signal correction for heart rate variability and coronary artery calcification in exercise cardiology, as well as out-of-distribution regression on distributed acoustic sensor data, social media text analysis for depression, and qualitative research on educational robots.

name: Thilina Dhanushka Kalahe Pathirana
summary: Thilina Dhanushka Kalahe Pathirana works on security and dependability of 5G mobile networks and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) systems that support mission-critical services. His publications cover a survey of joint security and dependability modeling, a two-level analytical model for estimating the availability of 5G-MEC systems under different redundancy settings, and the use of threshold secret sharing with trust-based node selection to protect and keep edge-stored data available.

name: Tormod Drengstig
summary: Tormod Drengstig studies mathematical models of biomolecular feedback systems, focusing on basic and antithetic controller motifs that are used as building blocks for regulatory networks. The work applies structural identifiability analysis across a large set of motif structures to show how model complexity and the choice of concentration or flow measurements determine whether parameters can be uniquely determined. The results support model building and experimental design in systems biology where measurable outputs are limited.

name: Trygve Christian Eftestøl
summary: Trygve Christian Eftestøl's publications apply machine learning and deep learning to biomedical signals and images, including MRI for Alzheimer's and prostate cancer, histopathology slides for bladder cancer, and cardiac MRI. The work also analyzes defibrillator and ECG recordings from in-hospital cardiac arrest and newborn resuscitation, using statistical survival models, prediction models and dimensionality reduction. Further studies cover cell-free DNA for cancer detection, heart rate variability and coronary calcification, and a systematic review of wearable cueing devices in Parkinson's disease.

name: Vinay Jayarama Setty
summary: Vinay Jayarama Setty works on automated fact-checking and misinformation detection, covering claim detection, claim normalization, evidence retrieval, stance detection and claim verification with large language models. His work includes benchmarks and datasets for numerical claims and real-world retrieval, studies of sparse and compressed retrieval, test-time scaling and multi-task fine-tuning, and tools for live and multilingual audio and podcast fact-checking. He also co-organizes the CLEF CheckThat! shared-task labs on multilingual fact-checking.

name: Yao Lu
summary: Yao Lu applies deep learning to medical imaging, Alzheimer's disease risk prediction, remote sensing object detection and IoT-based time series forecasting. The work includes segmentation of prostate MRI under varying scan protocols, normative modelling and multimodal embeddings that combine brain MRI with routine clinical variables, and an improved YOLOv8 detector for aerial imagery. Other publications cover smart home energy prediction with edge computing, transformer and LSTM models and explainability methods, as well as stroke prediction from wearable EMG signals.

name: Øyvind Meinich-Bache
summary: Øyvind Meinich-Bache works on AI-based analysis of video, audio and physiological signals to document and understand newborn resuscitation and birth events. His publications use deep learning, including 3D CNNs, vision transformers, vision-language models and thermal-video detection, to recognise resuscitation activities and time of birth, alongside clinical observational studies of stimulation and heart rate in the delivery room. He also addresses data collection, consent and privacy through blockchain-based consent management and a mothers' acceptability survey, with work carried out in Norway and Nepal.

name: A. H.Samitha Weerakoon
summary: A. H. Samitha Weerakoon studies decentralized and low-carbon energy systems, with a focus on micro gas turbines running on natural gas, hydrogen and blends, and on hydrogen systems combining electrolyzers, fuel cells and batteries. The work uses techno-economic assessment, Monte Carlo risk analysis, mixed-integer optimization scheduling, machine learning, digital twins, experiments and numerical simulation, including CFD of a floating wave energy converter. Application areas include microgrids in day-ahead electricity markets, shallow geothermal borehole heat exchanger design and field performance in different European climates, and wave energy.

name: A. Karimi
summary: A. Karimi studies the optimization and scheduling of multi-energy systems, using mixed integer linear programming models built at different levels of detail. The work compares how model fidelity affects computation time, energy imbalances and grid costs in a hospital case study. It shows how modeling key operational features, such as variable equipment efficiency and minimum on/off times, can give practical schedules without long solve times.

name: Alejandro Escalona
summary: Alejandro Escalona studies the geology of the Norwegian North Sea and Barents Sea, combining seismic interpretation, well logs, detrital zircon geochronology, organic geochemistry and basin and thermal modelling. His work covers Paleozoic basin evolution, sediment provenance and reservoir quality, and Jurassic source rock facies, as well as sequence stratigraphy in the Barents Sea. He also applies these methods to subsurface energy uses such as hydrogen storage in salt caverns, geothermal energy and CO2 storage, and to near-surface mapping and archaeological surveying with geophysical tools.

name: Ali Karimi
summary: Ali Karimi studies the design, operation and economics of small-scale and building-level energy systems, including cogeneration, trigeneration, waste heat recovery, battery storage and hydrogen-based multi-energy systems. The work uses simulation models tuned with measured demand data, techno-economic metrics such as payback, net present value and levelized cost of electricity, and Monte Carlo risk analysis, with case studies in hospital facilities. Related work covers control and energy management, including deep reinforcement learning for multi-energy systems and fuzzy control of solar PV and battery coordination in microgrids.

name: Anders Tokheim Hetland
summary: Anders Tokheim Hetland works on drilling engineering, focusing on estimating and controlling rate of penetration, drillstring vibration and downhole pressure. His work combines physics-based models such as lumped-mass drillstring dynamics and hydraulics with data-driven techniques including Ensemble Kalman Filtering, data analytics and rule-based control, tested through simulation and field data. The applications are real-time monitoring, drilling optimization, automation and detection of problems like kicks, lost circulation and packoffs.

name: Andrianifaliana Herimonja Rabenjafimanantsoa
summary: Andrianifaliana Herimonja Rabenjafimanantsoa studies multiphase and interfacial fluid flow, combining laboratory experiments, optical measurement and numerical simulation. Work includes laser-sheet imaging of capillary–gravity waves to estimate interfacial tension and viscosity, comparison of Volume of Fluid and Level Set solvers, and miscible displacement of shear-thinning fluids in a vertical channel. Application areas include non-intrusive liquid characterization for process monitoring and gas movement during well bullheading in drilling and well control.

name: Aqsa Batool
summary: Aqsa Batool works on chemistry and materials research spanning green extraction of plant bioactives, graphene-based adsorbents and electrocatalysts. Her publications cover deep eutectic solvent-ultrasound extraction of phenolics optimized with response surface methodology and neural networks, synthesis of poly(amidoxime)-grafted graphene oxide for removing hexavalent chromium from water, and hydrothermal preparation of graphite/iron oxide composites for methanol oxidation in fuel cells. Materials are characterized with FTIR, XRD, SEM and electrochemical techniques, and the work targets sustainable processing, water treatment and energy conversion.

name: Arash Mohammadi Vaniar
