summary: Arash Mohammadi Vaniar works on the operation and planning of power and multi-energy systems, combining machine learning, metaheuristic optimization and reinforcement learning. His publications cover battery remaining useful life prediction with gradient boosting, neural networks and physics-based models, degradation-aware scheduling of an agricultural microgrid, and distribution network reconfiguration with capacitor placement tested on IEEE benchmark feeders. He has also reviewed deep reinforcement learning in multi-energy systems and assessed the resilience of interdependent gas and electricity networks under multiple hazards.

name: Arild Saasen
summary: Arild Saasen studies drilling fluids and well construction, focusing on the rheology and stability of oil-based and water-based muds, barite sag, and emulsion conditioning with shear guns. His work combines flow loop experiments, laboratory and field tests, CFD and analytical modelling of non-Newtonian annular flow, cuttings transport and hole cleaning. It also covers lost circulation materials, cement plug support tools, magnetic ranging for geothermal wells, and drilling waste handling.

name: Arnfinn Aas Eielsen
summary: Arnfinn Aas Eielsen works on improving the precision of digital-to-analogue converters by reducing quantisation error, element mismatch and glitch disturbances. His methods include dithering, noise-shaping, moving-horizon and model predictive control, and learning control, tested through simulation and experiments on commercial converters and custom low-noise measurement circuitry. He also applies these ideas to nanopositioning systems, including temperature estimation for protecting high-power piezoelectric actuators.

name: B. S. Aadnoy
summary: B. S. Aadnoy works on well design and drilling engineering, covering casing strength, drilling fluids, well barriers, trajectory planning and rate of penetration. His publications combine analytical and numerical models, optimization methods (genetic algorithms, Kalman filtering, extremum seeking), machine learning and laboratory or field case studies. Applications include extended reach and sidetrack wells, sour-service casing integrity, shale barriers, lost circulation control and real-time drilling monitoring.

name: Behzad Amiri
summary: Behzad Amiri studies underground hydrogen storage and geological CO2 storage, using compositional reservoir simulation, analytical modelling and sensitivity analysis on field cases such as Norne and Smeaheia. The work covers diffusive hydrogen loss through caprock, combining hydrogen storage with CO2-based enhanced oil recovery in producing fields, and techno-economic optimization of storage in aquifers with genetic algorithms. He also builds deep-learning surrogate reservoir models to speed up simulation and optimize CO2 injection in saline aquifers.

name: Bikash Adhikari

position.nb: Forsker i styring og regulering av digital til analog omformere svitsjede syst.

summary: Bikash Adhikari works on control and signal processing methods for improving digital-to-analogue converters, including model predictive and moving-horizon optimal quantisation, noise-shaping and digital calibration to counter element mismatch and non-linearity. He tests these methods through simulation and experiments on off-the-shelf converters. He also studies control of clustered networks, using singular perturbation and multi-time-scale modelling to analyse synchronization and design computationally efficient controllers with guaranteed cost.

name: Carita Augustsson
summary: Carita Augustsson studies the sedimentary geology of ancient continental and marginal-marine basins, with a main focus on the Paleozoic and Triassic of the Norwegian North Sea and wider northwestern Europe. Her work combines well and seismic interpretation, facies and palaeocurrent analysis, detrital zircon U–Pb dating and whole-rock geochemistry to reconstruct sediment sources, basin formation and tectonic setting. Applications include petroleum exploration and reservoir quality prediction, including machine-learning estimation of porosity and water saturation from well logs, as well as a deltaic coastline study in northeastern Mexico.

name: Dagfinn Søndenaa Sleveland
summary: Dagfinn Søndenaa Sleveland studies fluid flow in porous rock, combining core-plug experiments, analytical solutions and numerical simulation. The work examines forced and spontaneous water imbibition for oil displacement in water-wet sandstones, looking at how capillary forces, relative permeability and viscosity affect recovery and pressure behavior. It also applies the fluctuation dissipation theorem to thermally driven pressure fluctuations in fluid-saturated sandstone and chalk, linking molecular-scale effects to macroscopic flow.

name: Dan Sui
summary: Dan Sui works on vibration, acoustics and drilling engineering, combining physical modeling with machine learning and state estimation. Publications cover acoustic metamaterials, porous liners and composite panels for noise control, as well as drillstring dynamics, rate-of-penetration and wellbore pressure estimation, gas kick detection, directional drilling control and drilling automation. Methods include theoretical vibroacoustic models, field and laboratory experiments, neural networks, reinforcement learning, Kalman filtering and simulation, applied to pipelines, offshore drilling and machinery, and oil reservoirs.

name: Daniele Blancone
summary: Daniele Blancone studies underground hydrogen storage in Zechstein salt structures of the southern Norwegian North Sea. The work combines well log and seismic data, GIS-based mapping, the GeoH2 tool and machine learning to characterize salt bodies, map internal heterogeneities and estimate cavern numbers and storage capacity. The applications are balancing intermittent wind and solar power and supporting low-carbon energy systems and CO2 storage projects offshore Norway.

name: David Scott Hall
summary: David Scott Hall studies lithium-ion battery materials, with emphasis on Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes, electrolyte additives and the solid-electrolyte interphase on graphite. The work combines NMR, Raman and X-ray spectroscopy, operando methods (acoustic emission, atomic force and optical microscopy, gas sensing), mechanical testing and chemo-mechanical and finite-element modelling to examine degradation, lithium heterogeneity and surface coatings. Related work covers electrolyte formulation for high-energy cells and mixed-metal oxide films for water oxidation catalysis.

name: Elvin Mirzayev
summary: Elvin Mirzayev studies how injecting CO2-saturated brine into limestone changes rock properties in deep saline aquifers used for carbon storage. Laboratory coreflooding experiments with micro-CT imaging and acoustic and mechanical testing examine how permeability, pore pressure, injection rate, salinity and temperature affect wormhole formation, porosity, permeability and stiffness. The work also includes a review of methane seepage near offshore wells and plugging and abandonment practices.

name: Foster Dodzi Gomado
summary: Foster Dodzi Gomado studies cementitious sealing materials for oil and gas wells, focusing on granite-based geopolymers as lower-carbon alternatives to Portland cement for shallow, low-temperature cementing and for plug and abandonment. The work uses laboratory testing of hydraulic sealability, shear bond strength, linear expansion, compressive strength and calorimetry, along with microstructural characterization, to examine expansive additives, waste glass, and precursor particle size. It also includes a regulatory review of European standards alongside experiments on stacked versus continuous annular cement barriers for well abandonment.

name: Fredrik Skaug Fadnes
summary: Fredrik Skaug Fadnes works on data-driven modelling and optimization of energy systems, using artificial neural networks, predictive control, Modelica simulation and Taguchi-based design analysis. His publications cover microgrids with wind power, hydrogen storage and micro gas turbines, as well as heat pumps using sewage heat, seasonal thermal storage and phase change material cooling. Applications are mainly municipal and residential buildings and city energy plants, using real operational data to cut energy use, cost and emissions.

name: H. Sahebi

position.nb: forsker i intelligent og autonom boring

summary: H. Sahebi works on data-driven monitoring, control and optimization of drilling operations in the oil and gas sector. The publications combine machine learning, trend analysis, rule-based and extremum seeking control, and microservice software that links AI models and large language model agents to real-time drilling data, tested mainly in drilling simulators and with replayed field data. Related work covers 3D wellbore trajectory design and visualization for well planning.

name: Hans Joakim Skadsem
summary: Hans Joakim Skadsem studies well construction and well integrity, combining laboratory experiments, finite element and OpenFOAM CFD modeling, and pressure transient analysis. The work covers cement sheath sealing, microannulus leakage and repair, expanding cement additives, casing centralization, reverse-circulation cementing and fluid displacement in annuli and Hele-Shaw cells. Applications include oil and gas wells, plug-and-abandonment, geothermal wells, and drill string and bearing fluid dynamics.

name: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse
summary: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse studies energy use in buildings and the flexibility of electricity demand, with a focus on Norwegian residential and municipal buildings. The work combines load forecasting, scheduling of virtual batteries and electric vehicles under dynamic tariffs, building performance simulation, and comparison of measured with calculated energy from performance certificates. Related publications cover access to consumer energy data for researchers and electricity market design for power systems with very high shares of renewables.

name: Hibat Errahmen Djecta
summary: Hibat Errahmen Djecta works on AI-driven geosteering, the real-time steering of drilling trajectories under geological uncertainty. The publications combine generative adversarial networks, ensemble data assimilation, particle filters, dynamic programming and deep reinforcement learning to update subsurface models from logging-while-drilling data and recommend steering decisions. Work also covers sequence machine learning for probabilistic forecasting of layer boundaries, simulator-based validation, and interactive open-source demonstrations for hydrocarbon, geothermal and CO2 storage drilling.

name: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei
summary: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei works on modelling, simulation and optimization of energy systems, with a main focus on micro-gas turbines (including humidified and hydrogen-fuelled cycles) and on heat pumps, thermal storage and building energy use. His methods include physics-based and grey-box dynamic models, Modelica simulation, Taguchi and multi-objective optimization, and neural networks for condition monitoring and data denoising. Application areas include distributed power and heat generation, solar-assisted CO2 ground-source heating, phase change material cooling for residential buildings, and comparison of calculated and measured energy in municipal buildings.

name: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos
summary: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos studies enhanced oil recovery through Smart Water injection, tailoring brine chemistry to alter rock wettability in chalk, limestone and sandstone reservoirs. The work uses laboratory core experiments such as spontaneous imbibition and flooding, supported by surface and chemical analysis and geochemical simulation. It also examines how carbonated water interacts with reservoir and caprock minerals for CO2 storage, and how core restoration methods affect wettability reproducibility.

name: J. A. Aasen
summary: J. A. Aasen works on well integrity and barrier materials for oil and gas wells, covering both casing mechanics and cementitious sealing materials. The publications combine analytical stress calculations for oval, hydrogen-embrittled casing with laboratory tests of geopolymers and expansive additives, and characterization of aged field cement, using shear and hydraulic bond strength, expansion, calorimetry, microscopy and diffraction. The applications are zonal isolation, plugging and abandonment, and sour-service casing design in wells such as those on the Norwegian continental shelf.

name: J. Djuve
summary: J. Djuve's work addresses the use of rock-based geopolymers as a replacement for cement in oil and gas well construction. The publication describes designing and testing spacer fluids by tuning rheology with additives and surfactants, then measuring rheological compatibility, strength and heat evolution when the spacer and geopolymer mix. The work applies to mud displacement, zonal isolation and wellbore integrity.

name: Jassem Abbasi
summary: Jassem Abbasi studies multiphase flow in porous media, such as geological reservoir rocks, using physics-informed neural networks, numerical simulation and machine learning. The work covers forward and inverse modeling, history-matching of core-scale experiments (spontaneous imbibition, porous plate and centrifuge capillary pressure tests, fractured shale), and benchmarking of methods for shock and discontinuity handling. Applications include CO2 storage, hydrocarbon recovery, special core analysis, and permeability prediction for tight sandstones.

name: Jelena Popovic-Neuber
summary: Jelena Popovic-Neuber works on electrochemistry for batteries, focusing on solid and liquid electrolytes, electrode interphases and ion transport in lithium, sodium, potassium, magnesium and aluminium systems. Her methods include electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, galvanostatic polarization in symmetric cells, solid-state synthesis, and theoretical modeling of transference numbers. The work also covers measurement methodology for polymer electrolytes, binders for silicon and solid-state electrodes, and a human geography perspective on energy communities.

name: Jonas Grill
summary: Jonas Grill studies ion transport and interphase behavior in battery materials, covering alkali metal, silicon, magnesium and aluminum electrodes in contact with liquid electrolytes, as well as polymer and inorganic solid-state electrolytes. The work relies mainly on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, galvanostatic polarization and numerical modeling to determine quantities such as activation energies, charge transfer resistance, diffusion coefficients and cationic transference numbers. It supports the development of lithium, sodium, potassium and multivalent batteries, including solid-state cells and cation-conducting binders.

name: Kaan Kizmaz
summary: Kaan Kizmaz studies the electrochemical behavior of alkali metal electrodes (lithium, sodium, potassium) in contact with liquid battery electrolytes, using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and galvanostatic polarization in symmetric cells. This work examines interphase properties, charge transfer, diffusion and cationic transference numbers as functions of time, temperature and concentration. A separate strand covers polymer synthesis and self-assembly, where miktoarm block copolymers made by anionic and ring-opening polymerization are processed into nanoporous, redox-active templates and characterized by cyclic voltammetry.

name: Kasra Saberi Beglar
summary: Kasra Saberi Beglar works on the operation and control of multi-energy systems, covering deep reinforcement learning, load forecasting and optimization-based pricing. The publications include a structured literature review of reinforcement learning for energy management, a data-driven study of day-ahead forecasting and storage-based flexibility using data from a Norwegian student dormitory, and a bi-level optimization model for dynamic pricing between energy providers and consumers. Application areas are building and urban energy management, demand response, electric vehicle and battery scheduling, and tariff design.

name: Kate Lorna Powell
summary: Kate Lorna Powell studies sediment provenance and depositional systems in ancient continental basins, with a focus on the Permian Rotliegend Group of the Norwegian North Sea. Her work combines detrital zircon U–Pb geochronology, facies analysis, palaeocurrent data from wells and palinspastic restoration to trace sediment sources, transport pathways and tectonic influences. The results are applied to understanding how sediment origin affects reservoir quality and to predicting reservoir distribution in subsurface energy-related settings.

name: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland
summary: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland works on recovering critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries and on geological carbon storage. His publications cover laboratory leaching of black mass with citric acid and choline chloride deep eutectic solvents, including optimisation of process conditions and measurement of viscosity and pH. They also include core-scale experiments on how CO2 exposure changes porosity and permeability in Danish chalk, relevant to the feasibility of storing CO2 in carbonate reservoirs.

name: Kjell Kåre Fjelde
summary: Kjell Kåre Fjelde works on gas behavior in oil and gas wells, studying how gas moves, expands and builds pressure during well control and drilling operations. His work combines drift-flux transient simulation, analytical models and laboratory flow-loop experiments, covering bullheading, kick migration in closed wells and gas unloading from marine risers. The studies address safety and equipment integrity questions in well kill, managed pressure drilling and offshore drilling.

name: Kristian Gjerstad
summary: Kristian Gjerstad studies drilling fluid rheology and wellbore hydraulics, covering thixotropic and viscoelastic mud behavior, gel strength and stress-overshoot tests, and fluid density at high pressure and temperature. His methods include structural kinetic models fitted to rheometer data, fast polynomial density models, transient hydraulic simulation and physics-informed data-driven estimation from distributed downhole sensors. These are applied to real-time downhole pressure estimation, cuttings and hole-cleaning monitoring, kick and loss diagnosis, pressure surges and the effect of heave on tripping.

name: Lucas Volpi
summary: Lucas Volpi studies fluid flow and its interaction with solid bodies using computational fluid dynamics, mainly the lattice-Boltzmann method coupled with finite element and discrete element methods. His work estimates hydraulic forces and torques on moving drill-string components and examines whirling vibrations in Newtonian and non-Newtonian drilling fluids, comparing the results with reduced-order models. He also simulates how particle shape and fluid rheology affect particle transport, relevant to offshore drilling and biomedical settings.

name: Mahmood Fani
summary: Mahmood Fani studies how CO2 and carbonated water interact with reservoir rocks and fluids, with a focus on carbon capture, utilization and storage and on enhanced oil recovery. The work combines laboratory methods such as core flooding, spontaneous imbibition, mineral exposure tests with SEM, EDX and ion chromatography, and geochemical and wellbore simulation (PHREEQC, Eclipse E300). Application areas include sandstone and chalk reservoirs, caprock and storage integrity, CO2 injection operations such as Northern Lights, and microfluidic pore-scale study of chemical oil recovery.

name: Mahmoud Khalifeh
summary: Mahmoud Khalifeh's publications cover well integrity and sealing materials for oil, gas and CO2 storage wells, including plug and abandonment practice, remedial treatment fluids and drilling fluid stability. Much of the work uses laboratory testing of mechanical, hydraulic sealing, rheological and microstructural behavior, plus pore-scale numerical and thermodynamic modeling, to study rock-based geopolymers and cement under downhole and CO2-exposed conditions. Related studies address low-carbon binders made from industrial by-products, regulatory review of well abandonment and methane seepage, and leaching of critical metals from battery black mass using deep eutectic solvents.

name: Masoumeh Amiri Mikal
summary: Masoumeh Amiri Mikal works on oil-based drilling fluids, focusing on how shearing affects emulsion quality and the stability of the fluid. Her publication reports field use of a dual jet shear gun in an offshore Norway drilling operation and tests at a drilling fluid plant, measuring electric stability and rheology to assess droplet size and prevent barite sag. The work combines operational field data with plant testing and offers an explanation for the observed effects.

name: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir
summary: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir works on well design and drilling engineering, covering drilling fluids, hydraulic optimisation, geomechanical evaluation and casing design, along with digital tools such as AI, real-time monitoring, predictive modelling, downhole sensors and autonomous drilling. His publications also include analytical modelling of pressure build-up in closed wells during gas kick migration, checked against transient drift-flux simulations, with attention to liquid compressibility and kick size. The work applies to petroleum drilling, well control and managed pressure drilling.

name: Mohammad Mansouri
summary: Mohammad Mansouri studies decentralized and multi-energy systems, with work on gas turbine performance modeling, hydrogen-fueled micro gas turbine health monitoring and fault diagnosis, and techno-economic and life cycle assessments of biogas, solar PV and hydrogen-based systems. His methods include physics-based simulation, machine learning and deep reinforcement learning, mixed integer and heuristic optimization, and Monte Carlo risk analysis. Application areas include building and residential flexibility, distribution network operation, rural bioenergy, and industrial energy use.

name: Mohsen Assadi
summary: Mohsen Assadi works on low-carbon energy systems, covering hydrogen technologies, micro gas turbines, shallow and deep geothermal energy, microgrids and wave energy converters. His methods include experiments and field testing (hydrogen micro gas turbine tests, electrolyzer and fuel cell trials, thermal response tests, monitored borehole plants), numerical modelling such as CFD and digital twins, and optimization, machine learning and Monte Carlo risk analysis. Applications include day-ahead market scheduling, techno-economic feasibility of hybrid and multi-energy systems, borehole heat exchanger design, residential energy management, distribution network reconfiguration and reuse of oil and gas wells for heat.

name: Mojtaba Ghaedi
summary: Mojtaba Ghaedi studies subsurface storage of hydrogen and CO2 in porous rock, covering capillary sealing, caprock and salt cavern leakage, density-driven convection, diffusion, and geochemical reactions with minerals such as calcite and pyrite. His methods include analytical formulations, PHREEQC geochemical and reactive transport modeling, reservoir simulation (e.g., Norne field), Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, pressure-decay diffusion experiments, and literature reviews. He has also applied modeling to calcite scaling in geothermal wells and appears as an author on biomedical studies of a nanoparticle-loaded amniotic membrane for burn healing and of dexmedetomidine during surgery.

name: Mostafa Mohammadi
summary: Mostafa Mohammadi studies the quality of pre-drill forecasts used in petroleum exploration, covering both geological probability of success and prospect volume estimates. Using historical prospect data from the Norwegian Continental Shelf, the work applies forecast verification measures such as the Brier score, skill score and reliability diagrams to detect bias, overconfidence and miscalibration. It also develops simple calibration approaches, including reference class benchmarks and distribution adjustments, to improve exploration decision-making and portfolio evaluation.

name: Nestor Cardozo
summary: Nestor Cardozo works on subsurface geoscience, combining seismic interpretation, well-log analysis, structural and numerical modelling, and machine learning to characterize faults, salt structures and reservoirs. His studies, largely in the Norwegian North Sea and Barents Sea, cover seismic inversion, salt cavern suitability for hydrogen storage, geothermal thermal modelling, fault and fracture prediction, and ensemble-based structural model building. He also statistically evaluates petroleum exploration volume and probability forecasts, studies seismic attenuation linked to fault fluids in Colombia, and develops discrete element software for tectonic deformation.

name: Nisar Ahmed
summary: Nisar Ahmed works on quantitative seismic inversion for reservoir characterization, developing pre-stack and amplitude-versus-offset methods that use adjoint-state gradients and quasi-Newton optimization to estimate elastic, viscoelastic and rock-physics properties. He applies these methods, and compares them with supervised deep learning approaches such as convolutional and transformer networks, to North Sea field data, including time-lapse monitoring of saturation and pressure for production and CO2 storage. His work also covers seismic facies and architecture of the Indus fan, reservoir geomechanics and pore pressure prediction in the Potwar Plateau, and seismic hazard analysis against building codes in Pakistan.

name: Pål Østebø Andersen
summary: Pål Østebø Andersen studies multiphase flow in porous media, combining numerical and analytical modeling with physics-informed neural networks for history matching and inverse problems. His work covers spontaneous imbibition, saturation functions, fractured rock and capillary pressure testing, and extends to underground hydrogen storage, CO2-enhanced oil recovery, aquifer thermal energy storage and geothermal tracers. Applications use reservoir simulation, including the Norne field model, along with optimization and uncertainty analysis for storage design and subsurface energy operations.

name: Qian Zhang
summary: Qian Zhang studies thermal energy systems for buildings, including CO2 heat pumps, solar-assisted ground-source heating, borehole thermal storage and phase change material cooling. The work uses Modelica simulation, Taguchi and grey relational optimization, techno-economic analysis, and deep learning models for forecasting and control, plus CFD-style analysis of rotating flows in flywheel energy storage systems. Applications include space and water heating in cold climates, district heating, residential cooling, geothermal borehole performance prediction and flywheel thermal management.

name: R. G. Hanea
summary: R. G. Hanea works on ensemble-based methods for decision making under uncertainty in subsurface reservoir management. The publication uses the EVEREST optimization tool and an approximate gradient (StoSAG) as a sensitivity measure to rank which geological and operational uncertainties most affect field-development and well-planning decisions. The approach is demonstrated on a synthetic reservoir model (REEK) for oil and gas applications.

name: R. I. Korsnes
summary: R. I. Korsnes studies the mechanical and geochemical behavior of subsurface rocks and wellbore materials using laboratory triaxial testing, core flooding, and microscopy and diffraction analysis. The work covers chalk and carbonate reservoirs (brine-rock reactions, mineral precipitation, water weakening, temperature cycling, and chemical strengthening for fracturing), creep behavior of impure Zechstein salt for hydrogen storage caverns, and granite-based geopolymers as sealing materials for wells. Applications include improved oil recovery, CO2 and hydrogen storage, geothermal wells, and wellbore integrity.

name: Raoof Gholami
summary: Raoof Gholami studies subsurface energy storage and geothermal systems, with a focus on underground hydrogen storage and CO2 storage, including gas mixing, dissolution, leakage, caprock sealing, geochemical reactions and salt cavern behaviour. The work combines numerical and analytical modelling, PHREEQC reactive transport, laboratory measurements of diffusion and rock mechanics, and review studies. It also covers shallow geothermal borehole heat exchanger design and operation, and calcite scaling in geothermal wells, using field and plant data from sites in Norway, Portugal and the USA.

name: Reidar B. Bratvold
summary: Reidar B. Bratvold works on decision analysis for subsurface energy projects, with a strong focus on geosteering, where drilling trajectories are adjusted sequentially under uncertainty. His methods include reinforcement learning, particle filters, approximate dynamic programming, deep neural networks, Bayesian optimization and real options valuation, as well as statistical studies of expert behavior and of forecast calibration. Applications include well placement, reservoir production optimization, petroleum exploration forecasting on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, energy transition investments such as offshore wind, and multi-criteria decision frameworks.

name: Rune Wiggo Time
summary: Rune Wiggo Time works on fluid mechanics, combining optical measurement of liquid properties with numerical simulation of multiphase and fluid–structure flows. His publications develop and validate a laser-sheet imaging method that uses capillary–gravity waves and inverse ray-tracing to estimate interfacial tension and viscosity, and compare Volume of Fluid and Level Set simulations of capillary waves. He also applies lattice-Boltzmann and finite element models to estimate hydraulic forces and vibrations on drill-strings and tool-joints in Newtonian and non-Newtonian drilling fluids.

name: Sadegh Ahmadpour

position.nb: Stipendiat i hydrogen lagring i porøse medier

summary: Sadegh Ahmadpour studies fluid transport and reactions in porous subsurface formations, with a focus on underground hydrogen storage and CO2 storage. The work combines numerical simulation, including PHREEQC reactive transport and advection-dispersion models, with new mathematical formulations and laboratory pressure-decay measurements of gas diffusion in water and brine. Topics include hydrogen dispersion and loss, density-driven convection, hydrogen sulfide formation from pyrite and sulfate reactions, cushion gas selection, and multiphase relative permeability.

name: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi
summary: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi studies granite-based geopolymers as alternatives to Portland cement for sealing wellbores in geological carbon storage. The work combines laboratory exposure to CO2, CO2-saturated water and brines under downhole pressure and temperature with mechanical testing, permeability measurements, microstructural and chemical analysis, and a pore-scale reactive transport model of carbonation. Related work covers testing standards for geopolymer sealants, a review of geopolymer sealant optimization, and nanocomposite drilling fluids assessed with core flow tests and CT imaging.

name: Siv Marie Åsen
summary: Siv Marie Åsen studies how thermo-thickening associative polymers flow through porous rock for enhanced oil recovery. Using laboratory flow experiments in sandstone and sand, the work measures how the resistance factor (mobility reduction) changes with associative content, salinity, temperature, flow velocity, time and sample size. The findings relate to polymer injectivity and sweep efficiency in oil reservoirs.

name: Skule Strand
summary: Skule Strand's publications address enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage in porous reservoir rocks such as chalk, limestone, sandstone and diatomite. Using laboratory methods including spontaneous imbibition, core flooding, mineral-brine reactivity tests, microscopy and geochemical modelling, the work studies wettability alteration with tailored Smart Water brines, polysulphate additives, ionic liquids and carbonated water. Applications include North Sea chalk fields, produced water reuse, and the integrity of reservoir and caprock minerals during CO2 injection.

name: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz
summary: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz studies energy systems and thermal-fluid engineering, combining experiments with numerical modelling. The publications cover techno-economic and risk assessment of micro gas turbine combined heat and power units running on natural gas and hydrogen blends in Norway, a periodic counterflow heat exchanger for heat and moisture recovery in building ventilation, and CFD-validated flow measurement with multi-hole orifices in turbulent pipe flow.

name: Steinar Evje
summary: Steinar Evje works on mathematical modeling and numerical methods for partial differential equations, with a recent focus on learning unknown flux and diffusion functions of nonlinear conservation laws from observed data. His methods combine symbolic neural networks with entropy-satisfying discrete schemes, and also use Bayesian inversion with ensemble Kalman filters. He applies these to multiphase flow, gas leakage along wells in CO2 storage settings, and continuum models of tumor progression and interstitial fluid pressure in cancer.

name: Sverre Ekrene Ohm
summary: Sverre Ekrene Ohm studies petroleum geochemistry and source rocks on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, including North Sea and Barents Sea basins. The work combines organic petrography, Rock-Eval, stable carbon isotopes, biomarkers and trace-metal analysis of core samples and oils to interpret depositional environment, organofacies and oil origin, and also includes seafloor mapping and seismic interpretation of methane-emitting mud volcanoes in the Barents Sea.

name: Tale Egeberg Aasland
summary: Tale Egeberg Aasland studies fluid flow using direct numerical simulation, mainly vortex dynamics, shear layer behaviour and flow regimes around straight and curved tandem cylinders at moderate to turbulent Reynolds numbers. More recent work combines laboratory experiments with OpenFOAM simulations to examine displacement of one fluid by another, including shear-thinning fluids, in a horizontal annulus with a washout section. The work is relevant to bluff-body flow and fluid forces on slender structures, and to annular displacement flows such as those in well operations.

name: Tina Puntervold
summary: Tina Puntervold studies enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage in chalk, limestone, sandstone and diatomite reservoirs, focusing on wettability, capillary forces and rock-brine interactions. Her laboratory work uses spontaneous imbibition, core flooding, mineral and brine analysis (SEM, EDX, XRD, ion chromatography) and geochemical modelling to test modified brines, carbonated water, additives such as polysulphate, ionic liquids and nanoparticles. The applications are North Sea and other reservoirs, produced water reuse, and the suitability of outcrop rocks as analogues for reservoir material.

name: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo
summary: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo studies heterogeneous catalysis over silver, focusing on the sub-reactions involved in the industrial conversion of methanol to formaldehyde. Using an annular structured reactor and repeated scanning electron microscopy imaging, the work links CO and hydrogen oxidation activity to changes in catalyst surface structure under different gas mixtures and steam levels. The findings help separate the effects of temperature and feed composition on silver restructuring and clarify reaction pathways in formaldehyde production.

name: V. N. Lima
summary: V. N. Lima studies the performance and durability of oil well cement and other barrier materials used for zonal isolation and well plugging and abandonment. Using laboratory and full-scale experiments, including triaxial and push-out mechanics, seepage and tracer tests, rheology and pipe viscometry, and microstructural analysis, the work covers expanding additives, fiber reinforcement, acid-gas (CO2 and H2S) degradation, rock-cement interfaces and microannulus repair. Related work on fiber-reinforced and waste-modified concrete examines flexural and cyclic behavior.

name: Veronika Abdulina
summary: Veronika Abdulina studies how mineral composition and pore structure control fluid storage, wettability and reactivity in subsurface rocks such as diatomite and chalk, with relevance to enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage. She also investigates hydrated iron sulfate minerals and related synthetic compounds, using in situ single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis and magnetic measurements across wide temperature ranges and low vacuum, including conditions relevant to Mars. Her reservoir work combines petrophysical and mineralogical characterization, imbibition tests and precipitation kinetics experiments.

name: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull
summary: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull develops seismic inversion methods, mainly pre-stack amplitude-versus-offset inversion that uses adjoint-state gradients and quasi-Newton optimization to estimate elastic properties, attenuation, and time-lapse saturation and pressure changes. The work also covers seismic forward modelling and imaging (salt bodies, fault imaging, migration velocity analysis, full waveform inversion), deep learning compared with physics-based inversion, and near-surface surveys with autonomous vehicles, sonar and GPR. Applications include North Sea reservoirs and CO2 storage, the Barents Sea, the Japan Trench, and archaeological and urban sites in Norway.

name: Yasaman Cheraghi
summary: Yasaman Cheraghi studies sequential decision-making under uncertainty in the energy sector, applying reinforcement learning, particle filtering and Monte Carlo methods. Her work includes automated geosteering systems benchmarked against human experts, statistical analysis of a large geosteering experiment, and investment and real option valuation for energy transition. She has also built neural network classifiers for screening enhanced oil recovery methods using data from past projects.

name: Zhixin Yu
summary: Zhixin Yu's publications cover materials chemistry for energy and environmental applications, including electrocatalysts for water electrolysis, CO2 and nitrate reduction, and CO2-to-methanol and zeolite-catalysed reactions. Related work designs interfaces and protective layers for zinc and sodium metal battery anodes, ion-selective membranes for lithium extraction by electrodialysis, and electrospun or composite films characterised by positron annihilation spectroscopy. Methods combine materials synthesis, electrochemical and spectroscopic characterisation, and density functional theory or molecular dynamics simulation, with one paper on hyperchaotic systems for DNA-encoded image encryption.

name: Åsmund Aamodt Resell
summary: Åsmund Aamodt Resell studies the mechanics of slender rods and pipes in curved and irregular boreholes, and the fluid flow in the annular gaps around them. The work combines beam theory and finite element modelling, for example for drill strings and casing with centralizers, with analytical solutions and computational fluid dynamics for flow and forces in eccentric annuli. The applications are well construction and drilling, with links to journal bearings and biomedical annular geometries.

name: Øystein Arild
summary: Øystein Arild studies well integrity in permanent plugging and abandonment, focusing on how annulus cement behind casing is qualified as a barrier under the NORSOK D-010 standard. His work examines the 30 m cement length requirement and compares continuous with stacked bond log evidence, using flow and capillary pressure calculations alongside qualitative assessment of cracking and failure. He has also developed a method to evaluate missing-data imputation in real-time drilling logs by estimating bounds on the coefficient of determination.

name: Guizhou Wang
department: Faculty of Science and Technology (department not stated)
summary: Guizhou Wang studies cryptocurrencies, monetary systems and sustainable finance using game-theoretic models, differential-equation and stochastic simulation models, econometric estimation, and bibliometric reviews. The work covers competition between hard, fiat, digital and central bank currencies, Bitcoin price dynamics, interest rate determination, and the economics of Bitcoin mining in biorefineries. It also examines volatility spillovers among ESG-rated stocks in China and the development of green finance research, with implications for policymakers, financial institutions and investors.

name: Abhishek Banerjee
summary: Abhishek Banerjee studies TiFe alloys for solid-state hydrogen storage, focusing on how niobium doping changes crystal structure and hydrogen uptake. The work combines arc-melting synthesis, in situ synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction, EXAFS and hydrogen absorption measurements to link structure with activation and sorption kinetics. The findings are relevant to stationary hydrogen storage and the design of new storage materials.

name: Aksel Hiorth
summary: Aksel Hiorth works on modeling fluid flow and chemical processes in porous media and on computational hemodynamics. His publications use physics-informed neural networks, lattice Boltzmann simulation with multiple relaxation time operators, pore-scale image-based simulation, geochemical and reactive transport modeling (IORSim), and laboratory zeta potential and imbibition experiments. Applications include oil recovery and low-salinity waterflooding in carbonates, fractured reservoirs, field-scale reservoir simulation with CO2 footprint estimates, and cardiovascular problems such as wall shear stress, coronary flow reserve and venous assist pumps for Fontan patients.

name: Aleksi Kurkela
summary: Aleksi Kurkela works on the equation of state of dense matter in neutron stars, using Bayesian inference, Gaussian-process priors, and constraints from chiral effective field theory, perturbative QCD, gravitational-wave and X-ray observations to probe possible quark-matter cores. He also studies the early out-of-equilibrium stages of heavy-ion collisions with QCD kinetic theory, including jet quenching, heavy-quark diffusion, hydrodynamization attractors, a parton cascade code and neural-network evaluation of collision integrals. Related work covers transport properties such as the bulk viscosity of quark matter, using perturbative and holographic methods.

name: Alex Bentley Nielsen
summary: Alex Bentley Nielsen works on gravitational wave astronomy, using Bayesian parameter estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data to test general relativity and to study black hole ringdown. His work includes searching for multiple ringdown modes and overtones in events such as GW190521 and GW150914, testing post-Newtonian phase corrections and the black hole area theorem, and constraining modified-gravity models including pseudo-complex GR and dirty black holes. He also develops waveform and analysis tools, such as line-of-sight acceleration corrections for compact binary signals and an effective-field-theory Lagrangian for the Kalb-Ramond field.

name: Alexander Rothkopf
summary: Alexander Rothkopf works in theoretical and computational physics, covering lattice QCD, hot nuclear matter and variational formulations of classical mechanics and gravity. His work includes reconstructing spectral functions from lattice data, studying heavy quarkonium and the static quark potential in the quark-gluon plasma, and modelling quarkonium as an open quantum system. He also develops action-based numerical methods that preserve symmetries and conserved charges, and simulation strategies for real-time quantum fields using complex Langevin dynamics with machine learning.

name: Alexander Ulanovskii
summary: Alexander Ulanovskii works in harmonic and complex analysis, focusing on sampling and reconstruction in shift-invariant spaces, Paley-Wiener and Bernstein spaces, and Gabor frames generated by Gaussian, hyperbolic secant and related functions. His publications use function-theoretic and density-based methods to establish sharp sampling conditions, to study the geometry of unit balls (extreme and exposed points), and to analyse completeness of exponential systems and the stability of shifts and atomic measures. Application areas include signal reconstruction, mobile sampling along curves, and time-frequency analysis.

name: Anders Tranberg
summary: Anders Tranberg studies out-of-equilibrium quantum field theory, with a focus on real-time dynamics in the early Universe, including reheating after inflation, bubble nucleation, stochastic inflation and instabilities in SU(2) gauge theory. His methods include numerical lattice simulations of Kadanoff-Baym equations from 2PI effective action truncations, classical-statistical simulations, and Lefschetz thimble Monte Carlo techniques for real-time path integrals. He also applies these approaches to quantum corrections for solitonic objects such as Q-balls.

name: Bjørn Henrik Auestad
summary: Bjørn Henrik Auestad's publications span sports cardiology and psychiatry. In cardiology, studies of middle-aged recreational athletes use echocardiography, cardiac troponin measurements and coronary imaging to examine how prolonged high-intensity exercise affects heart function, myocardial efficiency and non-obstructive coronary disease. In psychiatry, work includes a randomized trial comparing electroconvulsive therapy with pharmacological treatment in bipolar depression using patient-reported outcomes, and a registry-linked longitudinal study of suicidality trajectories in first-episode psychosis analyzed with growth mixture modelling and regression.

name: Daniil Krichevskiy
summary: Daniil Krichevskiy works in theoretical particle physics, mainly using chiral effective field theory and chiral perturbation theory to describe strongly coupled QCD-like gauge theories. He derives higher-order (NLO and NNLO) expressions for pion masses, decay constants, condensates and scattering, and fits them to lattice data for Sp(4) gauge theory to constrain pionic dark matter scenarios such as SIMPs. His other work covers large-charge and large-N effective field theory of the unitary Fermi gas, and an earlier optimal-filtering algorithm for correlating gravitational-wave and neutrino detector data to detect Galactic collapsing objects.

name: David Ploog
summary: David Ploog works in the representation theory of algebras and triangulated categories, focusing on simple-minded collections, simple-minded systems and bounded t-structures in cluster categories of acyclic quivers. His work uses categorical methods to establish bijections linking these objects to noncrossing partitions of Weyl groups. The results are theoretical and extend earlier results known for Dynkin quivers to the broader acyclic case.

name: Eirik Eik Svanes
summary: Eirik Eik Svanes studies the mathematical structure of heterotic string compactifications, focusing on moduli spaces, deformation complexes and cohomology for SU(3), G2 and related backgrounds, with a focus on supersymmetric vacua and anomaly cancellation. The work uses differential and algebraic geometry, generalised geometry, and holomorphic and topological field theories (including Kodaira-Spencer-type gravity and Chern-Simons theories) with one-loop calculations based on analytic torsion. Related papers cover moduli space metrics, effective field theory for gravity with a Kalb-Ramond field, Deligne cohomology for real line bundles, and discrete symmetries in five-dimensional superconformal theories.

name: Enrico Riccardi
summary: Enrico Riccardi works on computational modelling and machine learning, combining molecular simulation with statistical learning. His molecular work uses path sampling and molecular dynamics to study rare events such as drug unbinding from kinases, crystal phase transitions and thin film rupture in emulsions, and includes development of the PyRETIS software. He also applies regularised regression, random forests, neural networks and reinforcement learning to immune receptor data, histology images of fish livers and CO2 storage injection planning.

name: Eva Rauls
summary: Eva Rauls studies how macrocyclic supramolecular materials, especially pillar[n]arenes and dyn[4]arenes, capture and separate CO2 and other polluting gases. Her work combines density functional theory and tight-binding calculations with experimental synthesis, recrystallization, spectroscopy and gas adsorption measurements under dry and humid conditions. She has also used radio frequency scanning tunneling microscopy to probe dielectric relaxation in a single-molecule junction.

name: Germano Nardini
summary: Germano Nardini works on gravitational waves from the early universe and from compact binaries, with a focus on forecasting what the LISA space detector and other future observatories can measure. His publications use template-based signal reconstruction pipelines, Bayesian parameter inference, population modelling and Gaussian-process acceleration of inference, and also include theoretical work on phase transitions in warped extra-dimension models. Applications include inflation, cosmic strings, first-order phase transitions, primordial black holes, stellar-mass black-hole binaries and links to collider and pulsar timing array data.

name: Gøran Jan Nilsen
summary: Gøran Jan Nilsen's research uses inelastic and quasi-elastic neutron scattering, often with polarization analysis, together with complementary bulk measurements, simulations and density functional theory. One strand studies frustrated and quantum magnets such as pyrochlores, spinels, honeycomb magnets, altermagnets and rare-earth crystal field systems, working out their spin dynamics and exchange interactions. A second strand applies polarized neutron spectroscopy and Bayesian analysis to molecular motion in liquids, mixtures and protein solutions, and a third covers instrument development such as polarized neutron imaging and thermal transport in perovskites.

name: Helena Kolešová
summary: Helena Kolešová works in theoretical particle physics and cosmology, studying dark matter and strongly coupled dark sectors. Her publications use chiral effective field theory (fitted to lattice data), thermal field theory and cosmic-ray propagation and scattering calculations. They cover pion and glueball dark matter, cosmic-ray-boosted sub-GeV dark matter and its detection in experiments such as DUNE and Xenon-1T, early-universe reheating and phase transitions with gravitational wave signals, and the chiral soliton lattice in QCD.

name: Helge Paul Ruddat
summary: Helge Paul Ruddat works on mirror symmetry and enumerative geometry, using logarithmic and relative Gromov-Witten theory, tropical geometry, scattering diagrams and theta functions. His publications relate curve counts on log Calabi-Yau surfaces and local Calabi-Yau threefolds to period integrals, open mirror maps and Landau-Ginzburg potentials, and extend these relations to higher genus and to topological vertex computations. He also studies degenerations and smoothings of toroidal crossing spaces, SYZ fibrations, and algebraic structures that compute tropical curve multiplicities.

name: Jan Terje Kvaløy
summary: Jan Terje Kvaløy is a statistician whose publications apply survival analysis, regression modelling and cumulative sum monitoring methods to health registry and clinical cohort data. The work covers nationwide registry studies of liver and pancreatic surgery, intensive care and vascular outcomes, and clinical studies in long-COVID, dry eye, breast cancer ctDNA and newborn care. It also includes trial and cost-effectiveness analyses of a maternal and newborn care programme in Tanzania.

name: Jimmy Huy Tran
summary: Jimmy Huy Tran works on statistical methods for monitoring survival outcomes in health registries, developing cumulative sum (CUSUM) charts built on relative survival and excess hazard models to detect changes in survival time distributions while accounting for risk factors and uncertain cause of death. He also works on computational statistics, comparing adaptive tuning approaches for diagonal scale matrices in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo using numerical studies of sampling efficiency. Application areas include cancer registry surveillance and Bayesian sampling methodology.

name: Jörn Schulz
summary: Jörn Schulz works on statistical shape analysis, developing geometric representations such as skeletal models and elliptical tube models that keep objects valid and support mean shapes, hypothesis testing and analysis of joint variation across multiple objects. These methods are applied to brain structures such as the hippocampus and caudate in Parkinson's disease and autism. He also conducts clinical and epidemiological studies using regression and survival models on how orthostatic hypotension and sleep patterns relate to cognitive decline and dementia.

name: Konstantinos Alektoridis
summary: Konstantinos Alektoridis studies carbon dioxide capture using computational chemistry. His publication uses density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) calculations to compare how two functionalized dyn[4]arene macrocycles adsorb CO2, including binding inside the cavity and the uptake of multiple molecules until saturation. The work applies to materials for greenhouse gas capture and climate mitigation.

name: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen
summary: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen works in algebraic geometry, studying moduli spaces of geometric objects through Bridgeland stability conditions. His publication examines how the moduli space changes across walls, starting from the Hilbert scheme of pairs of skew lines in projective 3-space, and uses Mori theory to show the resulting spaces are smooth and projective. The work is theoretical and concerns the birational geometry of Hilbert schemes and related moduli spaces.

name: Olena Zavorotynska
summary: Olena Zavorotynska studies functional inorganic materials, including hydrogen storage alloys and hydrides (TiFe, magnesium borohydride) and zirconium and cerium metal-organic frameworks. Her work relies on synchrotron X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption, Raman and infrared spectroscopy, often applied in situ to follow how materials form, transform or decompose. Application areas covered include solid-state hydrogen storage, CO2 and other gas adsorption, silver recovery from solution, and energy-efficient mechanochemical synthesis of oxides.

name: Quoc Duy Ho
summary: Quoc Duy Ho studies materials mainly through first-principles computation (density functional theory, hybrid functionals, tight-binding, molecular dynamics and machine-learning force fields), with some experimental work on synthesis and gas adsorption. The work covers gas capture in pillar[5]arene frameworks, including CO2 adsorption and selectivity under dry and humid conditions. It also covers the electronic, magnetic and thermal properties of doped graphene, germanene and penta-graphene nanostructures, and point defects and dopants in wide-band-gap semiconductors such as β-Ga2O3 and ZnS for optoelectronic uses.

name: Sigbjørn Hervik
summary: Sigbjørn Hervik works in pseudo-Riemannian geometry, studying left-invariant metrics on Lie groups and the structure of Lie algebras through group actions and the moving bracket approach. His work also covers the construction of new Einstein spaces by deforming symmetric ones, using scalar polynomial curvature invariants and (para-)Kähler structures. The research is mathematical and theoretical, with results in classification and explicit examples across different metric signatures.

name: Tomas Brauner
summary: Tomas Brauner works in theoretical physics on effective field theories, spontaneous symmetry breaking and scattering amplitudes. His publications use field-theoretic and geometric methods, including soft bootstrap and recursion techniques, to study amplitude structure, dualities between theories, Nambu-Goldstone bosons and dipole symmetries, and also nonrelativistic systems. He also applies chiral effective theory to dense QCD matter in magnetic fields, mapping phases such as chiral soliton lattices and vortex lattices, and has written a book and teaching article on related topics.

name: Tore Selland Kleppe
summary: Tore Selland Kleppe develops Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms for Bayesian computation, focusing on Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, the No-U-Turn Sampler, step-size and scale tuning, Riemann manifold metrics, randomized numerical integrators and sampling on constrained domains. Methods are tested on multiscale and high-dimensional distributions and on hierarchical models, with supporting theory and software. He also applies Bayesian state-space and stochastic volatility models and economic modelling to commodity and oil markets, covering futures curves, volatility regimes and storage.

name: Tyson Ritter
summary: Tyson Ritter works in several complex variables, studying proper holomorphic embeddings of multiply connected domains into the complex plane. The publication builds parametric versions of the Andersén–Lempert procedure and Carleman-type approximation so that whole continuous families of domains can be embedded at once. The work is theoretical and rooted in complex analysis and approximation theory.

name: Adugna Deressa Akessa
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Adugna Deressa Akessa studies additive manufacturing of polymers, fiber-reinforced composites and metals, linking process parameters to mechanical behavior and microstructure. The work combines mechanical testing, fracture and microstructure analysis, heat treatment, numerical simulation and Gaussian Process Regression machine learning to predict and optimize properties of printed parts. Materials examined include PLA+, carbon fiber with Onyx, Inconel 625 made by wire arc additive manufacturing, and 17-4 PH stainless steel.

name: Anders Sagvåg Birkemo
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Ayushi Rai
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ayushi Rai studies thermochromic vanadium dioxide (VO2) thin films, including VO2/TiO2 bilayers, grown by pulsed laser deposition on substrates such as quartz, glass, silicon and LSAT. Her work links nanoscale structure, strain, grain morphology and phase composition to the metal–insulator transition and to electrical and optical switching, using transmission electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, tip-enhanced and confocal Raman spectroscopy, and electrical measurements. The application focus is energy-efficient smart window coatings.

name: Bjørn Helge Hjertager
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Bjørn Skaare
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bjørn Skaare's publications address the dynamics and marine operations of offshore wind turbines, covering both bottom-fixed and floating concepts. The work uses time-domain and frequency-domain simulations, finite element soil modelling, potential-flow hydrodynamics and analytical stability derivations to study monopile decommissioning with a crane barge, platform motions and crew workability, and aerodynamic motion instabilities. It also includes a review of decommissioning methods for bottom-fixed foundations.

name: Bruno Villoria
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bruno Villoria studies fatigue of welded details in long-span suspension bridges, focusing on orthotropic steel and aluminium bridge decks under multiaxial, non-proportional and variable-amplitude loading. The work develops and compares assessment methods, including grain scale plasticity-based models, equivalent structural stress and strain approaches with path-dependent cycle counting, and new damage accumulation rules, validated against published fatigue tests. It also applies finite element analysis and time-domain simulation of stochastic traffic and wind loading to case-study bridges to estimate the fatigue life of critical joints.

name: Chern Fong Lee
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Chern Fong Lee studies floating offshore wind turbines and combined wind and wave energy systems, using fully coupled time-domain numerical simulation to assess platform motions, mooring line tensions and power production. The work covers mooring design for intermediate and deep water (including synthetic rope, shared moorings and snap loads), dynamic power cables, extreme response statistics, simplified aerodynamic modelling, and mooring damage detection from vibration signals. Related work addresses wind turbine upscaling and a CFD-based analysis of piggyback pipelaying under current loads.

name: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi studies low-carbon cement binders, mortars and concrete in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and ground granulated blast furnace slag. The work combines laboratory testing of strength, shrinkage, workability and heat of hydration with microstructural and mineralogical analysis (SEM, XRD, FTIR, TGA, calorimetry), and also uses response surface methodology to build predictive mix-design models. The application area is reducing clinker use and CO2 emissions in construction while keeping mechanical performance.

name: Dimitrios Pavlou
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dimitrios Pavlou works on the mechanics and structural integrity of steel and offshore structures, covering multiaxial and machine-learning-based fatigue life prediction, hydrogen-assisted cracking in pipeline steel, and corrosion failure statistics for gas pipelines. His methods include analytical derivations (energy methods, dynamic models), finite element and CFD (OpenFOAM) simulation, mechanical and fractographic testing, and data analysis. Application areas include welded tubular joints, beams with web openings or corrosion, offshore wind turbines, nature-based living breakwaters for coastal protection, and structural health monitoring of marine structures.

name: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema works on manufacturing and materials engineering, covering natural fiber (enset) polymer composites, 3D printing, carbon nanotube-reinforced aluminum composites, and machining and welding of metals. His methods include experimental testing, microscopy, finite element simulation, response surface methodology, Taguchi design, genetic algorithms and machine learning for process optimization. He also applies structural equation modeling and literature reviews to study how additive manufacturing affects supply chains, especially in Ethiopian footwear firms and textiles.

name: Espen Undheim
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Espen Undheim works on laser-based directed energy deposition, a metal additive manufacturing process, applied to super duplex stainless steel. The publication uses Taguchi-designed experiments and weighted grey relational analysis to optimise process settings such as laser power, deposition speed, pulse frequency and shielding gas flow. Builds are assessed through density measurement, tensile testing, electron microscopy and diffraction to link process parameters with melt pool shape, porosity, microstructure and ductility.

name: Even Englund
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Even Englund studies the fatigue behaviour and structural integrity of welded steel tubular structures, with a focus on closely spaced and repair girth welds in S355 steel. The work combines laboratory fatigue testing to produce S-N curves, digital image correlation and strain gauge measurements, residual stress assessment by sectioning and X-ray diffraction, and finite element and continuum damage modelling. Applications include offshore structures, pipelines, wind turbine towers and oil and gas piping, including the effect of post-weld heat treatment on low-alloy steel pipe strength.

name: Gerhard Ersdal
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Gerhard Ersdal works on safety and risk in structural engineering, with a focus on assessing existing structures and offshore installations. His publications review risk-informed and probabilistic decision-making under uncertainty, discuss how safety should be managed for mooring systems as a whole system with barriers, and analyse reported incident data from semisubmersible units on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. The work combines conceptual critique with analysis of regulatory incident reports for offshore and structural safety.

name: Guang Yin
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Guang Yin works on computational and data-driven modelling of marine and offshore hydrodynamics, using CFD (mainly OpenFOAM and SedFoam), lumped-mass models, surrogate models, neural networks and physics-informed neural networks. The publications cover aquaculture systems (dissolved oxygen in fish cages and vessel tanks), ship and trimaran resistance, subsea pipelines and cables (scour, vortex-induced vibration, wave-current boundary layers, snap loads) and mooring optimization for floating offshore wind turbines. The work is aimed at early-stage design and risk assessment for offshore aquaculture, shipping, subsea infrastructure and floating wind.

name: Hadi Pezeshki
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hadi Pezeshki works on the fatigue and structural dynamics of engineering structures, with two main strands. One develops stress analysis methods, experiments and damage models to predict fatigue life under proportional and nonproportional multiaxial loading. The other develops analytical and numerical models of offshore monopile wind turbines, covering wave loading, soil-structure interaction, natural frequencies and gyroscopic effects, and he has also reviewed structural health monitoring methods for offshore and marine structures.

name: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu's research centers on additive manufacturing and materials engineering, covering natural-fiber and bio-based polymer composites for FDM, SLA and direct-ink-writing 3D printing, 4D-printed PLA, and wire arc additive manufacturing of Inconel 718. Methods combine mechanical, thermal, microscopy and X-ray diffraction testing with finite element, Monte Carlo and thermodynamic modeling. Application areas include bone tissue scaffolds with triply periodic minimal surface geometries, energy-absorbing honeycomb and foam structures, aluminum nanocomposites, and boiler tube thermo-structural analysis.

name: Idriss El-Thalji
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Idriss El-Thalji studies maintenance engineering and asset management, with a focus on predictive and risk-based maintenance for wind turbines and offshore oil and gas assets. His work combines vibration-based machine learning and deep learning (fault detection, remaining useful life forecasting) with agent-based and other simulation models of system availability, spare parts and offshore logistics, alongside wind-tunnel tests of blade erosion. He also publishes on maintenance management practice under Industry 4.0 and the green transition, and on gamified active learning in engineering education.

name: Jakob Emanuel Beer
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jakob Emanuel Beer studies the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies in logistics, with a focus on warehousing. The publication provided uses a systematic literature review of 56 documents to build a conceptual framework linking the factors that influence adoption, the benefits companies can achieve and the barriers they face. The work takes the perspective of companies adopting the technologies and is relevant to both academics and logistics practitioners.

name: Jan Frick
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan Frick studies logistics and supply chain management, with a focus on resilience, customs compliance, and digital information flows in cross-border trade. The work combines conceptual framework and reference-architecture design, scenario and sensitivity analysis, literature reviews, expert interviews and an empirical warehouse case study. Application areas include maritime chokepoint disruption, AI-supported document handling, EU product passports and carbon border rules, 3PL warehouse storage, collaborative freight exchanges, and blockchain in the energy sector.

name: Jan Magne Nygård
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan Magne Nygård works on predicting oil recovery in layered, heterogeneous reservoirs under water, gas and water-alternating-gas injection. The work uses a large set of black oil reservoir simulations and physics-informed machine learning, in which least square support vector machine models are trained with optimizers such as particle swarm, genetic algorithm, grey wolf and gravitational search. It is applied to enhanced oil recovery, including how mobility ratios, gravity effects and hysteresis affect recovery.

name: Jan-Tore Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Jarle Berge
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jarle Berge studies the structural behavior of aluminum columns, focusing on global buckling of extruded rectangular hollow profiles made from the 6082-T6 alloy. The work combines laboratory compression and cyclic loading tests, with digital image correlation to track deflection and strain, and compares the results with Eurocode 9 and Euler buckling calculations. It applies to structural design and code assessment for aluminum construction, including the safety margins in current design rules.

name: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen studies wind effects on long-span bridges, buildings and offshore structures, using wind tunnel tests, full-scale field monitoring with sonic anemometers, lidars and pressure sensors, and numerical simulation including large eddy simulation. Related work covers fatigue of welded steel and aluminum bridge details under combined wind and traffic loading, atmospheric boundary layer wind profiles and turbulence for floating wind turbines, and ship and barge collisions with bridges. Application domains include bridge design, structural health monitoring, urban pedestrian wind comfort and wind energy.

name: Jawad Raza
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jawad Raza studies how best practices in asset management and safety can be defined, qualified and transferred between industries, with a focus on oil and gas and road tunnels. The work draws on literature review and analysis of published best practice definitions, and proposes a transfer model based on a systems-theoretic approach. It is relevant to industrial asset owners and standardization bodies seeking consistent criteria for adopting practices across sectors.

name: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage studies how operators of complex, high-risk industrial systems can detect and make sense of process deviations early, using concepts such as advanced situation awareness, contextual knowledge and hybrid decision-support solutions. The work draws on conceptual analysis, review of industrial cases and collaboration with industry, with applications in remote operations, rotating machinery in oil refineries and digitalized industrial assets. It also covers asset management, including industrial agility as a strategic capability for asset-centric organizations in industrial eco-systems.

name: Jianan Zhang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jianan Zhang develops numerical models of floating dock operations, representing the dock and docked vessel as six-degree-of-freedom rigid bodies under hydrostatic, hydrodynamic, mooring and contact loads, with hydraulic models of ballast water systems. The work covers automatic ballast control with a modified P-controller, stability and structural bending analysis, and simulation of failure cases such as valve or pump faults and corroded ballast tanks. Model-scale and full-scale tests are used to validate the models, and earlier work includes finite element simulation of ice floe sliding impact on ship hull structures.

name: Jon Erik Karlsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jon Erik Karlsen studies how metal additive manufacturing and rapid casting can supply on-demand replacements for obsolete or undocumented components on ageing offshore installations on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. His work combines literature review, a roadmap and flow chart for the on-demand supply chain, and a multi-criteria decision analysis (Analytic Hierarchy Process) with industry expert input, applied to a valve body case from Statfjord-A. The outputs are intended for energy, oil and gas asset owners, suppliers and engineers.

name: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson studies wind engineering and structural dynamics of long-span bridges, using full-scale monitoring with sonic anemometers, surface pressure sensors and Doppler lidars, along with wind tunnel tests, finite element modelling and system identification. Work covers bridge deck aerodynamics, buffeting loads, wake and turbulence characteristics, vibration control under wind and seismic hazards, and floating bridge response to non-uniform winds. Related studies address offshore and urban wind measurement, satellite and CFD wind data, floating offshore energy platforms, FRP-concrete interfaces and ground heat exchangers.

name: Kenneth Alasdair Macdonald
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Kjell Tore Fosså
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Kjell Tore Fosså studies low-carbon cement-based materials, focusing on replacing large shares of cement with silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and blast furnace slag. The work uses compressive strength tests, calorimetry, SEM and XRD, shrinkage measurements, and response surface modelling to link hydration, microstructure and mechanical performance in pastes, mortars and high-strength concrete. He has also carried out large-scale experiments and nonlinear finite element simulations of crack spacing in reinforced concrete members.

name: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus works on computational and experimental fluid dynamics, using CFD (including RANS, LES, OpenFOAM and lattice Boltzmann methods), wind tunnel and laboratory experiments, and machine learning surrogate models. His applications include urban pedestrian wind comfort, sports aerodynamics such as cycling, and non-Newtonian and multiphase flows in Hele-Shaw cells, annuli and thin films. He also applies deep learning and optimization to wind energy, covering turbine blade and bearing condition monitoring, leading-edge erosion, and floating offshore wind power cable design.

name: Lennart Vogt
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lennart Vogt studies atmospheric boundary layer wind and turbulence for wind energy, using lidar remote sensing, sonic and cup anemometers, and reanalysis data. His work compares analytical wind profile models with offshore and near-coastal observations under different atmospheric stability conditions, and characterizes turbulence spectra and spatial coherence. He also applies these profiles to simulate the motions of a floating wind turbine and has used nacelle lidars to measure flow in an urban campus setting.

name: Lichao Xiong
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lichao Xiong studies the hydrodynamic behaviour of offshore renewable energy structures, with a main focus on membrane-type floating photovoltaic platforms tested as 1:40 scale models and compared with numerical simulation. The work also covers coupled numerical modelling of floating offshore wind turbines, including a two-rotor turbine with wave energy converters and a simplified aerodynamic model, as well as laboratory and finite element tests of pile foundations for offshore wind. Applications include mooring design, sea-state response assessment, simulation efficiency and foundation capacity for offshore solar and wind systems.

name: Lin Li
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lin Li studies the dynamics, design and reliability of floating offshore structures, including floating wind turbines, offshore fish farm cages and multi-body marine systems. The work combines time-domain hydrodynamic and mooring simulation, Kriging surrogate models, sensitivity and reliability analysis, and faster ODE solving schemes with analysis of metocean and wind data (hindcast and lidar). Applications include shared mooring design, aquaculture-wind co-location, installation operations such as jacket lift-off, and site conditions for floating wind arrays.

name: Lorents Reinås
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lorents Reinås works on the safety and structural integrity of offshore drilling operations, covering subsea wellhead fatigue, drilling riser loads and dynamic positioning of mobile drilling units. His work combines global riser simulations, structural reliability analysis, incident data collection and statistical frequency estimation, and it includes the development and assessment of wellhead load relief equipment. It is applied to Norwegian Continental Shelf drilling, standards such as NORSOK U-001, and operating and disconnect criteria.

name: M. K. Samarakoon
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: M. K. Samarakoon studies low-carbon cementitious materials, focusing on mortars in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and silicon manganese slag, an industrial byproduct. The work uses compressive strength testing over 3 to 56 days, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and isothermal calorimetry to assess strength, microstructure and heat development. The application area is sustainable construction, aiming to cut clinker use and CO2 emissions where fly ash is becoming less available.

name: Madushan Madhava Jayalath
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
