summary: Stanislav Stedronsky studies how higher education can support sustainability, focusing on the competencies students need to act as change agents in line with the Sustainable Development Goals. His work links Education for Sustainable Development with theories of sustainability transitions and uses an exploratory case study of Norwegian universities to identify obstacles to competence-based teaching. It also examines a novel simulation game as a practice-oriented teaching tool.

name: Terje Hillesund
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Terje Hillesund studies how people read and write scholarly and digital texts, drawing on theories of embodied and distributed cognition and on affordance theory. His work uses observational interviews with academics to examine how reading, writing and digital publishing are linked through printouts, screens and online tools. He also develops conceptual frameworks that treat the body, the text's material form and technology as parts of one reading process.

name: Tevfik Murat Yildirim
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Tevfik Murat Yildirim is a political scientist who studies legislative behaviour, political communication, public opinion and gender in politics, with a strong focus on Turkey, the UK and the US. His work combines large-scale datasets, including parliamentary speeches, news coverage and decades of survey responses, with text coding, panel and regression models, causal designs such as difference-in-differences, and survey experiments. Application areas include voter turnout, women's political careers, media attention to politicians, emotive rhetoric, policy priorities, and partisan reactions to misinformation and elite cues.

name: Thomas Michael Sattich
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Thomas Michael Sattich studies the politics and geopolitics of the energy transition, covering renewable energy policy, energy security, carbon capture and storage, and maritime and ocean infrastructure such as shipping, canals and port clusters. His work uses case studies, policy analysis and social research, with a focus on Norway, the Baltic Sea Region, Lithuania and Poland. He also develops and evaluates simulation games and competence-based approaches for teaching sustainability and climate negotiation in higher education.

name: Torvald Øgaard
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Torvald Øgaard studies how people experience and respond to service and work environments, using survey-based quantitative research and meta-analysis. His publications examine how perceived crowding and emotions shape satisfaction and loyalty among skiers at a ski resort, and how workplace incivility relates to employees' intentions to leave across sectors and countries. The work applies to tourism and visitor attraction management and to organizational and human resource settings.

name: Turid Borgen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Ugo Corte
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ugo Corte is a sociologist who develops theory on group culture, community and emotion, using qualitative and ethnographic evidence. His work examines how profanity builds belonging in workplaces such as war-zone trauma units, kitchens, wildfire crews and prisons, and how cruelty can become a source of shared pleasure in gangs, bullying and military settings. He also writes essays on sociological theorizing, anonymity, uncertainty and the legacy of Howard Becker's work on art worlds and collaborative circles.

name: Xia Sun
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Xia Sun studies gender and career advancement in higher education, focusing on how female researchers in Norway navigate institutional policies, gender roles, relationships and personal goals. The work uses empowerment as an analytical framework and draws on interview data to examine how structural and individual factors shape recognition and progression. It is relevant to institutional policy design aimed at supporting women's academic careers.

name: Yonas Tesema
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Yonas Tesema studies labour, industrialisation and land dispossession in Ethiopia, using ethnographic fieldwork in garment factories in the Bole Lemi Industrial Park to examine worker exploitation, shop-floor control, rural women's migration and displaced peasants. More recently he has used interviews and case studies in Stavanger, Norway, to examine industrial decarbonization, positive energy districts and stakeholder collaboration in the energy transition. His work links social and economic questions of fairness to development policy and sustainability transformation.

name: Aksel Leknes
summary: Aksel Leknes works on automated analysis of infant brain MRI, focusing on volumetry from ultra-low-field scanners that are more accessible in low- and middle-income settings. His publication presents an open-source segmentation pipeline built on age-specific templates and priors, checked against high-field MRI references using correlation and percentage-error measures across infant cohorts in South Africa and Uganda. The pipeline is applied to regional brain growth, sex differences and the effects of low birthweight in early development.

name: Aleksander Hagen Erga
summary: Aleksander Hagen Erga studies substance use disorders, particularly polysubstance use, using prospective longitudinal cohort studies in Norwegian treatment populations. His work covers how cognitive impairment, personality traits, childhood trauma, PTSD symptoms and drug-free friendships relate to recovery, psychological distress and life satisfaction, using regression, growth curve and dynamic structural equation models, and he leads a randomised trial protocol on dextroamphetamine substitution for amphetamine dependence. He also contributes to Parkinson's disease research, including an online trial of video-based cognitive behavioural therapy for depression, a survey of cannabis use, and a study of cognitive decline.

name: Aleksandra Sevic
summary: Aleksandra Sevic studies how people and workers respond to digital technology, covering attitudes toward and acceptance of artificial intelligence, and technostress and burnout among employees. Her work uses questionnaire surveys, regression and factor analysis, and scale translation and validation, as well as systematic reviews and meta-analyses on workplace health topics such as eHealth interventions and alcohol use in relation to sickness absence. Application areas include AI adoption and regulation, higher education workplaces, and occupational health.

name: Ayo Zahra
summary: Ayo Zahra develops and validates open-source image analysis tools for measuring brain volumes from ultra-low-field MRI in infants and toddlers. The work uses age-specific templates and priors for automated segmentation, compares results against high-field MRI with correlation and percentage-error measures, and applies mixed-effects models to examine age, sex and birthweight. The application focus is accessible infant neuroimaging in low- and middle-income settings, with cohorts in South Africa and Uganda.

name: Bianka Anna Karshikoff
summary: Bianka Anna Karshikoff studies how inflammation relates to pain, mood, anxiety and sickness behavior, combining clinical cohorts of people with chronic pain with experimental studies in healthy volunteers given low-dose endotoxin. Her methods include blood cytokine and multiplex protein profiling, questionnaire validation, brain imaging (MRI and functional connectivity), and body odor sampling with human ratings. The work addresses chronic pain, psychiatric comorbidity, response to behavioral treatment, and how the immune system affects perception and social behavior.

name: Danilo Garcia
summary: Danilo Garcia studies personality, well-being and mental health, often using Cloninger's biopsychosocial model, across student, clinical, older-adult and community populations. His work uses surveys, structural equation modeling, network analysis, psychometric validation and literature or policy reviews, and increasingly applies AI and language models to mental health assessment and therapy outcomes. Application areas include education, health-care training, physical activity and aging, school health, media psychology and sustainable food systems.

name: Francesco Margoni
summary: Francesco Margoni studies how moral reasoning, cooperation, fairness and ideas about leadership and authority develop from infancy through old age. His work uses looking-time experiments with infants and toddlers, child and adult behavioural tasks and surveys across several countries, and also covers research methods such as the violation-of-expectation paradigm and subjective logic. Applications include human-robot interaction and ethical decision-making among intelligence professionals.

name: Jone Ravndal Bjørnestad
summary: Jone Ravndal Bjørnestad studies mental health and substance use recovery alongside consumer behavior in banking. Work on psychosis risk, substance use disorders and contraceptive prescribing draws on systematic reviews and meta-analyses, qualitative interviews and focus groups, and longitudinal modelling such as latent class and dynamic structural equation models. Work on banking uses representative survey and longitudinal data with regression and moderated mediation analyses to examine how satisfaction and self-efficacy relate to bank-switching intention and behavior. Further work covers a gaming-based intervention for unemployed young adults and training for foster care counselors.

name: Lilla Magyari
summary: Lilla Magyari studies how brains process speech and vocal sounds, using EEG and event-related potentials in humans, dogs and pigs to compare neural responses across species and to test whether dogs understand object words. Her work also covers human speech in multi-talker settings, prediction and turn-taking in conversation, speech patterns in political speeches, and how reading on screen versus print affects text comprehension among vocational students.

name: Liv Sand
summary: Liv Sand studies eating disorders, personality disorders and perfectionism, and how these relate to depression and treatment outcomes in clinical and student populations. She also researches the epidemiology of potentially traumatic experiences and PTSD symptoms in Norwegian children and adolescents, using population surveys linked to national patient registry data and statistical methods such as latent class analysis and logistic regression. Her work also includes clinical case studies and commentaries on integrated and transdiagnostic psychotherapy, including cognitive behavioural therapy for eating disorders.

name: Marita Kallesten Brønnick
summary: Marita Kallesten Brønnick studies how hormonal contraceptives, especially the intrauterine system, are prescribed to adolescents and how this relates to mental health outcomes such as depression. Her work uses focus group interviews with healthcare professionals at Norwegian health centers, analysed thematically, to identify who is recommended which products and why. The findings are intended to help future quantitative studies account for selective prescribing as a source of confounding.

name: Muriel Marisa Katharina Bruchhage
summary: Muriel Marisa Katharina Bruchhage studies early brain development in infants and children, mainly using structural, diffusion and functional MRI, including ultra-low-field scanners for use in low- and middle-income settings. Her work combines image-analysis pipelines, normative and longitudinal statistical models, and machine learning to link brain volumes and connectivity to cognition, maternal factors, genetics, nutrition and the gut microbiome. She has also contributed to work on the cerebellum in ageing and cerebellar pathways, and to a preclinical rat MRI study of compulsive behaviour.

name: Nicolay Gausel
summary: Nicolay Gausel studies moral emotions, especially shame, and how they shape defensive or repair-oriented responses in close relationships, in social groups and around prejudice toward immigrants. His work combines conversation analysis of research interviews with young people who have committed sexual violations, experiments with university students, and psychometric testing of a therapy outcome-monitoring scale on a sample of Norwegian clients. Applications include social work practice, psychotherapy measurement and understanding social mobilization against prejudice.

name: Pravin Tembjerg
summary: Pravin Tembjerg studies how separating children and young people from their families affects them, and how family relationships can be rebuilt or reunification pursued. The work, which appears as chapters in an edited volume, compares separation contexts such as child protection removal, institutional care, parental incarceration, divorce, migration and parental death. It draws on attachment, crisis, recognition and other social theories and links separation to children's mental health, with relevance to child welfare and helping professionals.

name: Synne Wiberg
summary: Synne Wiberg studies how digitalization affects people working in Norway's offshore petroleum industry, focusing on psychosocial factors such as cognitive demands, trust and workload. Her work combines in-depth interviews with offshore personnel and a narrative review of government and industry reports to compare workers' experiences of digital tools like handheld devices with industry priorities. The research applies to high-risk work settings where efficiency, safety and employee well-being need to be balanced.

name: Tore Tjora
summary: Tore Tjora studies behavior, mental health and work-related outcomes in Norwegian populations using surveys, registry data, longitudinal designs and psychometric validation. His work covers consumer bank-switching and self-efficacy, adolescent emotion regulation and adversity, psychosis risk and substance use, and safety climate and work disability in the petroleum and welfare sectors. Methods include regression, structural equation and latent class or growth models, decision-tree machine learning, and qualitative focus groups.

name: Vendela Husberg-Bru
summary: Vendela Husberg-Bru studies hazardous alcohol use among middle-aged and older adults using data from the population-based Tromsø Study in Norway. Using cross-sectional analyses with logistic regression, chi-square tests and analysis of covariance, the work compares health behaviours and health-related quality of life between people with and without hazardous drinking, and examines how potentially traumatic events in childhood and adulthood relate to it. The findings inform public health understanding of alcohol-related risk in the general adult population.

name: Wenche Ten Velden Hegelstad
summary: Wenche Ten Velden Hegelstad studies early psychosis, covering first-episode psychosis, clinical high risk states and long-term recovery, using large international neuroimaging consortium data alongside longitudinal cohort follow-up, registry linkage, trajectory modelling, psychometric validation and systematic review. Her work also includes qualitative interview studies of recovery, help-seeking, service use and virtual reality therapy, and covers suicidality, childhood adversity, antipsychotic treatment response and family psychoeducation. Applications lie in early detection, mental health service delivery, and standardising recovery definitions and outcomes in psychosis research.

name: Aleksandar Bozic
summary: Aleksandar Bozic studies social work and child and family welfare, with a focus on community-based practice, NGOs, migration and child protection. His work uses qualitative interviews, scoping reviews and comparative analysis of programs and education laws across several European countries, as well as case-based descriptions of service models such as family group conferences. Application areas include international field placement in social work education, psychosocial support for children in transnational families, family reunification after child protection placement, anti-bullying efforts for immigrant pupils, and social innovation among NGOs in conflict-affected settings.

name: Anne Ingeborg Apeland Svalastog
summary: Anne Ingeborg Apeland Svalastog studies kinship foster care within child welfare systems, focusing on how caregivers and adolescents experience contact with child welfare services. Her work uses a qualitative evidence synthesis of published studies on caregiver perspectives and in-depth interviews with adolescents in Norway, interpreted through sociological ambivalence theory. The findings relate to social work practice and the support offered to kinship families.

name: Anne Katrine Folkman
summary: Anne Katrine Folkman studies how welfare and education services work with families, children and professionals, with a focus on Norway and Sweden. Her publications examine co-production and collaboration in child protection reunification, drawing on research, policy and practice, and teachers' experiences of distance teaching during COVID-19, using a survey and thematic analysis. Her work addresses organisational conditions such as management support, professional roles and inequality in service delivery.

name: Ayan Abdi Mohamoud Handulle
summary: Ayan Abdi Mohamoud Handulle studies how migrants and ethnic minorities, especially Somali Muslims in Norway, experience stigma, racialization, religious belonging and encounters with child welfare services. Using ethnography and qualitative interviews, she draws on Goffman's ideas of stigma and interaction ritual, together with bonding social capital, to explain everyday responses to discrimination and parents' fears of child removal. Her work also covers transnational family life, return migration and separation of migrant families, and connects to social work practice, cultural diversity and decolonial perspectives.

name: Brita Gjerstad
summary: Brita Gjerstad studies how digital and welfare technologies are introduced and used in healthcare, with a focus on Norwegian primary care and hospital settings. Her work uses qualitative methods such as semi-structured interviews, reflexive thematic analysis and a scoping review, and draws on care ethics, governance theory and socio-technical systems frameworks. Topics include collaboration between municipalities and technology companies, the effect of technology on professional care values and autonomy, and implementation of robotic-assisted surgery.

name: Cornel Maria Nesseler
summary: Cornel Maria Nesseler studies discrimination, gender and performance in sport and related social settings, mainly using field and online experiments such as emails sent under native- and foreign-sounding names, plus video-based perception experiments. He also applies econometric methods including regression discontinuity, ordered logit and causal random forests to topics like coach changes in tennis, ethnic bias in amateur sports clubs, welfare administration, housing and hiring. A further strand covers esports, including player performance during the war in Ukraine and a textbook on esports and society, as well as field testing of penalty-shooting strategies in youth football.

name: Eden Begna Gobena
summary: Eden Begna Gobena studies motherhood after imprisonment and the reintegration of formerly incarcerated women, with a focus on Ethiopia. Her work uses descriptive phenomenological interviews, a qualitative systematic review, and attachment-based analysis of mother-child contact, and it draws out implications for social work practice, non-custodial sentencing and prison policy. She also writes on decolonizing research methods and researcher training in social work from an African perspective.

name: Elisabeth Enoksen
summary: Elisabeth Enoksen conducts qualitative research in Norway on children, youth and vulnerable or minority groups, drawing on interviews and diary entries. Her studies cover social control in the friendships and romantic relationships of cross-cultural youth, survivors' decisions to seek redress for institutional childhood abuse, Sámi practitioners' nature-based cultural teaching, and children's everyday lives during COVID-19 school closures. The work applies frameworks such as social control theory, victim capital and Bronfenbrenner's ecological model to questions in social welfare, education and childhood.

name: Heidi Lie Eriksen
summary: Heidi Lie Eriksen studies social work education and practice, including international field placements, experiential teaching of vulnerability and solidarity, and community-oriented work with NGOs. Her methods include qualitative interviews with students, thematic analysis of survey responses, and a randomised field experiment with welfare frontline workers. Her work covers social work training in Norway and abroad as well as fairness in how the Norwegian welfare system treats applicants with foreign-sounding names.

name: Hulda Mjøll Gunnarsdottir
summary: Hulda Mjøll Gunnarsdottir studies social work and child welfare in Norway, including how social workers in criminal justice and other fields experienced working conditions, job satisfaction and resilience during COVID-19. Her work also covers young women with out-of-home care histories, kinship caregivers' experiences with child welfare services, social workers' emotion management in violent extremism prevention, school counselling and children's pandemic lockdown diaries. She uses surveys with regression analysis, mixed methods, qualitative interviews, narrative and diary methods, and qualitative evidence synthesis.

name: Håvard Haugstvedt
summary: Håvard Haugstvedt studies social work practice in Norway and security-related violence. His social work research uses interviews, focus groups, surveys and regression analysis to look at outreach youth work and substance use prevention, criminal justice social work, social workers' resilience and job satisfaction during COVID-19, and social workers' roles, emotions and support in preventing violent extremism. His security research draws on incident datasets and statistical analysis of open-source data to examine armed drone use by cartels and other violent non-state actors, civilian harm from drone attacks, and radicalization among people with military backgrounds.

name: Ida Bruheim-Escobar
summary: Ida Bruheim-Escobar studies how digital technologies are used in social work, including their effects on communication, documentation, decision-making and relationships between clients and social workers. Her work uses an umbrella review method to synthesise findings from 24 systematic reviews across areas such as child welfare, mental health, migration and elderly care. She draws on sociotechnical systems theory and ethics of care to examine ethical concerns, digital inequalities and the limited inclusion of service-user perspectives.

name: Ingunn Studsrød
summary: Ingunn Studsrød conducts qualitative social work research on family violence, child protection and marginalised women and young people, with a focus on mothers, survivors of abuse and people leaving state care or prison. Her studies use interviews, narrative and phenomenological methods, thematic analysis, a systematic review and a survey of teenagers, and draw on feminist, intersectional and attachment perspectives. The work covers settings in Norway, Poland and Ethiopia and addresses practice and policy concerns such as post-separation abuse, redress after institutional abuse, disclosure of violence, reintegration after incarceration and decolonial research training.

name: Ingunn Tollisen Ellingsen
summary: Ingunn Tollisen Ellingsen studies child welfare and social work, with a focus on foster care, kinship care, family reunification and professional decision-making in Norway, and also in Spain. Her work relies mainly on qualitative methods such as interviews, fieldwork, case document analysis, narrative and thematic analysis and evidence synthesis, along with Q methodology. It covers the perspectives of child welfare workers, foster parents, kinship caregivers, children in care and adolescent girls, including how standardised assessment tools are used and how young people experience substance use.

name: Ismail Seçer
summary: Ismail Seçer studies trauma and mental health in children, adolescents and adults, especially survivors of the 2023 Türkiye earthquakes, as well as school attendance problems and burnout among students and healthcare workers. His work combines psychometric scale adaptation, structural equation modelling, network analysis, latent profile analysis and meta-analysis with pilot intervention trials of a parent-child therapy adapted for disaster-related trauma. Application areas include clinical assessment, school-based prevention, cross-cultural comparison and disaster response.

name: Joakim Finne
summary: Joakim Finne studies how child welfare interventions are delivered in practice, with a focus on preventing child maltreatment in families with complex support needs. His work evaluates the implementation fidelity of a home-visiting programme called Family Partner, combining descriptive analysis of practitioner-reported routine data with thematic analysis of interviews and focus groups. The research informs how pilot trials and measures for complex public health and family support interventions are designed before full-scale randomized trials.

name: Kathrine Skoland
summary: Kathrine Skoland studies how Norwegian teenagers who have experienced physical violence from adult family members try to tell others about it. Using survey data from over 11,000 young people in the Local Youth Survey, she applies quantitative analysis to see who they confide in and how the frequency of violence, gender and socioeconomic background relate to disclosure. The work bears on child protection, school-based support and public policy on domestic violence.

name: Kolbjørn Kallesten Brønnick
summary: Kolbjørn Kallesten Brønnick studies human behavior, cognition and wellbeing across several fields. His work applies survey, longitudinal, regression and psychometric methods to bank-switching and self-efficacy in digitized consumer markets, digital stress and burnout among employees, health communication, and healthcare quality. He also conducts clinical neuroscience research, using resting-state EEG with data harmonization and machine learning, along with neuropsychological assessment, to study dementia, Parkinson's disease and cognitive outcomes in brain metastasis survivors.

name: Kristina Johansen
summary: Kristina Johansen studies the experiences of young unaccompanied refugees resettled in Norway, focusing on psychosocial well-being, family separation and reunification, and encounters with social workers, asylum policy and public attitudes toward immigration. Her work uses qualitative interview-based research and draws on recognition theory and perspectives on care. The findings address how youth-focused social services and welfare and immigration policies could better support these young people's well-being and family life.

name: Liv Jorunn Baggegård Skippervik
summary: Liv Jorunn Baggegård Skippervik studies child protection in Norway, focusing on how dialogue-based processes in child welfare tribunals can help children, parents and child welfare services reach shared solutions. Her work examines the use of these processes in reunification after compulsory out-of-home care, drawing on mediation theory and restorative practice and on the legal context shaped by European Court of Human Rights criticism. The analysis is conceptual and discusses strengths, limitations and directions for future research on child welfare practice.

name: Maren Sagvaag Retland
summary: Maren Sagvaag Retland studies abuse that continues after parents separate, with a focus on how custody, visitation and the reunification of families are handled when intimate partner violence is involved. Her work, set in a Norwegian context, reviews research evidence and legal questions through a literature-based approach. It is aimed at welfare professionals such as court officials, social workers and psychologists who work to protect children and parents.

name: Marita Wassbakk
summary: Marita Wassbakk studies criminal justice social work in Norway, focusing on the working conditions of social workers in correctional services and the needs of the people they support. Her work uses a mixed-methods survey design and applies the job demands–resources model to examine how infection control measures during COVID-19 affected workload, collegial contact and service delivery. The research is relevant to correctional services, social work practice and workforce wellbeing in crisis situations.

name: Marte Tonning Otterlei
summary: Marte Tonning Otterlei studies child protection and child removals in Norway, focusing on how parents and child welfare workers experience care order processes and on reunification after out-of-home placement. Her work uses qualitative interviews analysed with positioning theory and thematic analysis, alongside theoretical frameworks drawing on developmental psychology and psychotherapy to examine grief, stigma, imagination and continuing parent-child bonds. She also examines dialogue-based and restorative approaches in child welfare tribunals as ways to support reunification.

name: Mikhail Gradovski
summary: Mikhail Gradovski studies education and social research through the lens of dialogism, drawing on Bakhtin's ideas. His publications use qualitative approaches such as textbook analysis and historical accounts of student-founded democratic schools in Norway and Sweden, and he also examines how merged methods in social science can be developed with dialogic tools. Application areas include early childhood teacher education, international exchange between Norway and Russia, and democratic governance in schools.

name: Mira Aurora Marlow
summary: Mira Aurora Marlow studies the experiences of young women who have lived in out-of-home and residential care, focusing on how they construct identities, manage visibility and resist dominant labels. Her work uses narrative interviews, feminist listening-guide analysis and contextual analysis across macro, meso and micro levels, with an intersectional perspective. The findings are applied to social work practice, including wellbeing, user participation and collaborative services.

name: Morten Tønnessen
summary: Morten Tønnessen works across biosemiotics, ecological semiotics and phenomenology, drawing on Jakob von Uexküll's umwelt theory to study how humans and other animals experience and interpret their worlds, including past lifeworlds, animal welfare and interspecies translation. He also contributes to cross-cultural survey research on well-being, perceived economic inequality, power and status, and love and religiosity, as well as interview-based work on outdoor recreation in youth residential care in Norway. Further work uses Human Development Index data to assess how economic output relates to welfare and environmental pressure in the USA.

name: Reidun Ims
summary: Reidun Ims studies how paid work relates to the integration of immigrants in Norway's welfare state, and what this means for social work practice. Using an integrative review with systematic database searches and thematic analysis of 28 articles, the work examines immigrant labour market outcomes, women's workforce participation and gender equality, and discrimination in working life. The findings are applied to questions of welfare policy and qualification measures that could support higher immigrant employment.

name: Richard Michael Piech
summary: Richard Michael Piech studies children's and young people's family lives, including how siblings relate to one another after parental divorce and how children in Ghana take on caring roles for relatives. The work uses qualitative methods, namely semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis, with young people in Norway and Ghana. Findings are tied to practice, with recommendations for social workers and other supportive adults and a call for formal support for young carers.

name: Sarah Catherine Patricia Duff Hean
summary: Sarah Catherine Patricia Duff Hean researches social work and child and family welfare, with a focus on sibling relationships, child protection services, family separation and reunification, and the experiences of migrant and minority children. Her work also covers criminal justice and rehabilitation, including drug court participants, probation supervision and mothers after incarceration, as well as disability support in Tanzania. She mainly uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, thematic analysis and interpretative phenomenological analysis, alongside literature reviews, community-based participatory research and theoretical and methodological reflection on decolonizing research, in settings including Norway, Ethiopia and Tanzania.

name: Simone Grassini
summary: Simone Grassini studies how people perceive, trust and use artificial intelligence, drawing on psychometric scale development and validation, surveys, and preregistered online experiments. Applications include AI in higher education and military training, AI ethics, social robots, digital health acceptance and comparisons of AI and human creativity. He also works on environmental psychology and visual consciousness, using bibliometric mapping, implicit association tests and mental imagery tasks.

name: Sjur S. Sætren
summary: Sjur S. Sætren studies how childhood maltreatment and other adversities relate to adolescent mental and somatic health, with a focus on emotion regulation and affective inhibitory control. His work draws mainly on the large Norwegian UEVO population survey and uses generalized linear models, latent change score and network analysis, mediation analysis, and questionnaire validation. He also contributes to research on psychosis, including a systematic review of how childhood adversity is measured and a study of remission patterns in people at clinical high risk, and has examined adolescent health during the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Svein Erik Tuastad
summary: Svein Erik Tuastad studies how public-sector professionals contribute to preventing radicalisation and violent extremism in Norway, focusing on cooperation between municipal social workers, the police and the security service. Using qualitative methods, including in-depth and focus-group interviews analysed through Abbott's theory of professional jurisdiction, the work examines role clarity, confidentiality and the securitisation of social work. The findings relate to policy and practice in multi-agency prevention.

name: Thiago Medeiros da Costa Daniele
summary: Thiago Medeiros da Costa Daniele studies physical activity, aging and mental health, with a strong focus on public health in Brazil. His work combines literature reviews, a meta-analysis of rodent exercise studies, bibliometric mapping, policy document analysis, cross-sectional surveys of older adults and psychometric scale validation. Application areas include fitness programs, sarcopenia risk, social inequality in later life, teacher wellbeing and social media psychology.

name: Tina Bojovic
summary: Tina Bojovic studies how young people raised across more than one culture experience and handle social control in their friendships and romantic relationships. Her work in Norway uses qualitative research with 15 youths and a four-dimensional framework of social control, looking at the roles of parents, minority communities, peers and wider society. The research relates to youth, gender, ethnicity and religion, and questions culture-centred explanations of minority young people's relationships.

name: V. Heaslip
summary: V. Heaslip conducts research on the nursing and midwifery workforce, covering academic careers, advanced practice roles, social care nursing, retention in emergency care, and digital health leadership and record systems. Work also addresses health inequities, including racism towards Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities and decolonising midwifery education. Methods include systematic, scoping and integrative reviews, concept analysis, qualitative and mixed-methods studies, and clinical trials with embedded patient-experience and economic components in burn scars, ankle fracture, hip replacement and mental health social prescribing.

name: Wenche Hovland
summary: Wenche Hovland studies social work with children and young people in Norway, focusing on sibling relationships after parental divorce or removal into child protection care, and on how siblings take each other's perspectives. She also examines the expectations that young unaccompanied refugees and social work leaders hold of social workers in trauma-informed residential care. Her work relies mainly on qualitative interviews with thematic analysis, plus an integrative literature review and a chapter on podcasting for academic-practice collaboration.

name: Annet H. de Lange
department: NHS – Department of Leadership and Service Innovation
summary: Annet H. de Lange studies ageing workforces and sustainable employability, looking at how age, job crafting, personal values, autonomy and HR practices relate to work ability, vitality and career outcomes. Her work uses surveys, longitudinal and observational designs, latent class and regression analyses, scale validation, process evaluations and systematic reviews. Application settings include healthcare, elderly care, freight transport and high-hazard industries, with attention to workplace health promotion, bridge employment after retirement and age-related prejudice.

name: Christine Lundberg
department: NHS – Department of Leadership and Service Innovation
summary: Christine Lundberg researches popular culture tourism, including fan pilgrimage, film and literature tourism, and how destinations develop and sustain themselves around media phenomena. Her work uses scoping reviews, interviews, fieldwork, eye-tracking and conceptual analysis, and extends to event value co-creation, digital collaboration in destination management organisations, outdoor recreation foresight in the Nordic region, and how Swedish retail chains collaborate to support city center resilience.

name: Huseyin Arasli
department: NHS – Department of Leadership and Service Innovation
summary: Huseyin Arasli studies hospitality and tourism management, covering leadership, employee behavior and attitudes, service quality, and corporate governance. His work uses surveys analysed with structural equation and multilevel models, scale and index development, qualitative interviews, bibliometric reviews, and text and content analysis of online reviews, including machine-learning methods. Application areas include hotels, casinos, airlines, airports, service robots and virtual influencer marketing, with a focus on the Nordic countries, Turkey and Northern Cyprus.

name: Aaron Martin Cooper
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Aaron Martin Cooper studies how Arctic climate change and proposed climate interventions affect the rights of Indigenous Peoples. His work uses legal and governance analysis, drawing on international law, ocean law and climate science, to examine topics such as sea ice geoengineering, free, prior and informed consent, and the pressures from mineral extraction and renewable energy projects on Indigenous lands. The research applies to Arctic and Scandinavian governance, climate justice and the inclusion of Indigenous communities in decision-making.

name: Andrea Minto
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Andrea Minto studies financial regulation and financial innovation from a legal perspective, covering EU anti-money laundering law, crypto-assets and stablecoins, central bank roles, and banking supervision. The work uses doctrinal legal analysis of EU legislation and case law, sometimes combined with institutional and complexity frameworks, to examine bodies such as the new AML Authority, the ECB and central banks. Application areas include payment services, digital euro and CBDC, securities post-trading with distributed ledger technology, crypto exchange platforms, and compliance in professional football.

name: Bård Misund
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Bård Misund studies the economics of salmon aquaculture and of resource-based industries, covering industry clusters, innovation, market concentration, disease costs, offshore production strategies and price transmission in European markets. He applies econometric methods such as profit-persistence models, difference-in-differences and concentration indices, along with comparative investment analysis and case studies. His work also addresses regulation and taxation, including environmental rules, rent taxes and policy instruments in aquaculture and Norwegian petroleum, and links between carbon emissions reduction and company financial performance.

name: Dengjun Zhang
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Dengjun Zhang is an applied economist who studies seafood markets and firm behaviour, focusing on salmon demand, consumer preference shifts, price transmission and the economics of salmon farming. He uses econometric methods such as demand systems, hedonic price models, profit-persistence models, instrumental variables and Google Trends data, and applies them to household and auction data as well as to large cross-country firm surveys. His work also covers manufacturing and sustainability topics, including energy outages, credit constraints, green innovation, environmental activities of firms, temporary employment and climate-related behaviour.

name: Erika Christie Berle
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Erika Christie Berle studies how economic and social choices play out in energy, finance and organizations, using quantitative methods on large text and market datasets. Her work includes spatial regression of regional newspaper coverage to link wind turbine density with local narratives in Germany, event and return analysis of ethical exclusions by Norway's sovereign wealth fund, and linguistic analysis of Federal Reserve meeting transcripts to assess gender diversity in committee deliberations. Application areas include renewable energy acceptance, responsible investing and corporate governance.

name: Hamid Cheraghali
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Hamid Cheraghali studies financial distress and default prediction for small and medium-sized enterprises, using logistic regression and machine learning methods such as LightGBM and XGBoost on Norwegian and U.S. firm data, and has also reviewed the methodological literature in this area. He also works in empirical finance, using event analysis, volatility forecasting and Google search data to examine how cyberattacks, investor fear and consumer or investor attention relate to returns, volatility and fund flows in cryptocurrency, oil, luxury-goods and mutual fund markets.

name: Kristoffer Svendsen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Kristoffer Svendsen works on laser wakefield accelerators, using experiments, particle-in-cell simulations and Bayesian optimization to improve electron beam quality through control of laser spectral phase, focus, wavefront and plasma density profiles. He also develops laser-plasma lenses and uses the resulting x-rays for absorption spectroscopy of materials and for tomography of fuel sprays. His other work includes two-photon fluorescence imaging of spray atomization in fuel injectors, and legal studies of liability and compensation for offshore oil pollution.

name: Lana Bubalo
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Lana Bubalo studies private law, especially tort liability and personality rights, using doctrinal analysis of legislation and case law. Her work covers compensation for non-material damage under the GDPR as interpreted by the Court of Justice of the European Union, and the historical development of legal protection for honor and reputation. She also carries out comparative legal research on the legal cultures of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Serbia in the Western Balkans.

name: Marius Sikveland
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Marius Sikveland studies corporate finance, focusing on how firms fund themselves and how financing choices relate to profitability, using econometric analysis of firm-level panel data. His work covers political connections and access to government support and bank loans during COVID-19, ownership and profitability in Norwegian salmon aquaculture, and capital structure in the hospitality industry under seasonality and geographic clustering. The applications span crisis policy, aquaculture and tourism.

name: Ola Johan Settem
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Ola Johan Settem studies human rights law, focusing on how the autonomy of religious communities is balanced against the fundamental rights of the people they employ. His work analyses European Court of Human Rights case law on proportionality in disputes over loyalty requirements, such as limits placed on clergy marrying, and compares it with the approaches of other international tribunals. The research is doctrinal and legal-analytical, with relevance to religious organisations, employers and legal practitioners.

name: Tarjei Mandt Larsen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Tarjei Mandt Larsen works in epistemology and phenomenology, focusing on Husserl's theories of knowledge. His publications use close philosophical analysis of Husserl's texts to examine how perceptual experience can justify belief and what level of certainty is needed for cognition that aims to resolve epistemological problems. The work engages current debates in the epistemology of perception and metaepistemology.

name: Vegard Bø Bahus
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Vegard Bø Bahus studies how civil procedure and case law shape the development of animal law, with a focus on strategic litigation in the Nordic countries. His work uses a case study of Norway, including the Supreme Court's 2023 Dog Breeding Case, to examine how courts now accept abstract lawsuits about the general application of legal provisions. The research also notes comparable trends in other Nordic and continental European states.

name: William Gilje Gjedrem
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: William Gilje Gjedrem works on oral health among marginalized populations, with a focus on people living in prisons. The publication describes a multicenter randomized, double-blinded controlled trial in four prisons in Rogaland County testing whether motivational interviewing added to oral hygiene packages improves plaque scores, hygiene routines and related attitudes. The work is relevant to correctional services, dental practitioners and policy makers planning dental care for underserved groups.

name: Anders Åkerman
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Anders Åkerman studies international trade and labour economics, using Swedish and Norwegian firm-level and employer–employee data. His work uses quasi-experimental methods and theoretical models to examine how imports affect firms' carbon intensity, how market concentration shapes demand for college-educated workers and wage inequality, and how broadband adoption changes the effect of distance on trade.

name: Bernt Arne Ødegaard
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Bernt Arne Ødegaard studies empirical finance, covering ethical and ESG-based investing, corporate governance and the microstructure of equity markets. His work uses stock return, insider trading and trading venue data to examine portfolio exclusions by Norway's sovereign wealth fund, the effects of Norway's board gender quota on director informativeness, tick size competition among European venues, and the drop in market liquidity during COVID-19 margin increases. The findings relate to investors, regulators, exchanges and corporate boards.

name: Dora Zsuzsanna Simon
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Dora Zsuzsanna Simon studies the economics of climate policy, using a quantitative international trade model to examine how carbon pricing affects different countries. Her work compares efficient carbon taxes with alternatives such as international transfers and differentiated tax rates, assessing their effects on fairness between countries. The application area is the design of global climate policy and its distributional consequences for low-, middle- and high-income countries.

name: Elin Svensen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Elin Svensen studies how students' beliefs about whether intelligence is fixed or can grow relate to school achievement, family background and gender in Norway. Her work uses multilevel statistical modelling of data on thousands of students moving from lower to upper secondary school, looking at grades and completion of the first year. The findings bear on educational inequality and on how socio-emotional skills may support lower-performing students.

name: Eric Perry Bettinger
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Eric Perry Bettinger studies education and the economics of education, mainly through randomized field experiments and quasi-experimental policy evaluations, along with some survey and machine learning work. His projects cover socioemotional skills and growth mindset, informational and text-message nudges, computer-assisted learning, school day length, and college access, financial aid, dual enrollment and degree completion in the U.S., Brazil and Norway. He also works on research methods, including monitoring of trial fidelity, SMS-based measurement of student mindsets, and satellite imagery as a proxy for regional economic activity.

name: Gorm Kipperberg
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Gorm Kipperberg studies how people value environmental goods and trade them off against economic development, mainly using stated-preference methods such as discrete choice experiments, contingent valuation and mixed logit models. His work covers coastal and marine ecosystems, mining, aquaculture and wind energy in Norway, and also tests how survey design, scientific uncertainty, psychological ownership, place attachment and the passage of time shape stated preferences. He additionally contributes meta-analysis of willingness to pay for aviation emission reductions, and co-authored studies on biogas potential in Pakistan and agricultural carbon footprints in China.

name: Hammad Shaikh
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Hammad Shaikh studies how instructor emails can influence student behaviour in large introductory computer science courses, focusing on homework reminders and procrastination. The work uses randomized A/B experiments and factorial designs deployed in real courses, alongside email open-rate analysis and surveys and interviews with instructors and students. The findings inform how educators can test and design everyday communication to support homework completion and academic performance.

name: Ingeborg Foldøy Solli
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Ingeborg Foldøy Solli studies how education programs shape children's and adolescents' skills, using large randomized field experiments in Norwegian preschools and high schools. Her work examines structured and play-based preschool curricula, executive functions, gender gaps in early learning, and an online growth-mindset curriculum that affects students' choice of challenging high school math courses. Outcomes include math, language, executive functioning, course choices and graduation, with attention to differences between groups and settings.

name: Jean Paul Rabanal
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Jean Paul Rabanal conducts laboratory experiments in finance and economics, mainly on how exchange-traded funds, stock splits, and shareholder voting affect asset prices, trading, and firm policy choices. His work also covers individual and strategic decision-making, including dynamic portfolio choice, market entry and exit under different information disclosure rules, and whether correlated equilibria emerge in repeated games. Methods combine controlled experiments with theoretical modeling, nonparametric efficiency tests, and estimation of adaptive dynamics.

name: Kristoffer Wigestrand Eriksen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Kristoffer Wigestrand Eriksen studies how people behave when giving financial advice while their own interests conflict with those of the person advised. He uses large-scale behavioral experiments, including a binary dictator game adapted to an advice-giving setting, to compare advisor behavior with a baseline of direct decision-making. His work addresses moral behavior and fairness in financial advice markets.

name: Lassi Mikael Ahlvik
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Lassi Mikael Ahlvik studies the economics of environmental conservation policy, focusing on how land use restrictions affect property values. Using Finnish property transaction data linked to the staged rollout of the Natura 2000 protected area network, he estimates effects on forest, agricultural, unbuilt and built properties. The work examines the costs of conservation and how they are distributed across landowners, house and cabin owners, and areas with differing socioeconomic conditions.

name: Lijun Liu
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Lijun Liu studies the economics and sustainability of aquaculture and related natural-resource sectors. The work uses stochastic bioeconomic simulation to assess production, market and system-failure risks in recirculating shrimp farms, and indicator-based comparisons of environmental, economic and social performance across aquaculture systems, including in China. Further publications examine gender participation and influence in fisheries and aquaculture, and use survey data and regression analysis to explore Chinese consumers' attitudes toward certified wood products.

name: Marco Lambrecht
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Marco Lambrecht conducts experimental economics research on financial markets, strategic interaction and decision-making under risk. His laboratory and online experiments examine how Bitcoin-style mining affects price bubbles, how disclosing players' intelligence changes cooperation and coordination in repeated games, and how gender relates to participation in risky skill games. The work informs understanding of cryptocurrency pricing, behavioral game theory and gender differences in risk-taking.

name: Mari Rege
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Mari Rege studies education and human capital development in Norway, from preschool through high school, and also looks at supportive leadership in workplaces. Her work mostly uses large-scale field experiments and randomized trials, along with skill-building models, survey-based measurement and quasi-random assignment of students to classes. Topics include structured and playful preschool curricula, executive functions, gender gaps, additional classroom teachers, teacher relationship skills, and online growth-mindset programs that affect students' course choices.

name: Olga A. Rud
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Olga A. Rud conducts laboratory experiments in finance and economics, mainly on how exchange-traded funds, stock splits, and shareholder trading and voting affect asset prices, trading activity, and firm policy decisions. Related work covers individual choice and strategic behavior, including dynamic portfolio efficiency, entry and exit decisions under different information disclosure, and adaptive play in games with correlated equilibrium. Methods combine controlled market experiments, game-theoretic modeling, and nonparametric and simulation-based analysis.

name: Peter Molnar
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Peter Molnar studies financial econometrics and empirical finance, with a focus on volatility modelling and forecasting using range-based GARCH and multivariate correlation models, including applications to cryptocurrencies, oil and exchange rates. He also develops and compares statistical and machine learning methods (logit, LightGBM, XGBoost) for predicting SME default and financial distress, and uses difference-in-differences and event-style analyses to examine how taxes, infrastructure, cyberattacks and investor or consumer attention affect asset and house prices.

name: Radoslaw Lucjan Stefanski
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Radoslaw Lucjan Stefanski studies how governments should set the social discount rate used in cost–benefit analysis and public investment appraisal. His work uses a Ramsey-rule framework and historical patterns in real interest rates and growth to argue that pure time preference may decline over time, possibly through generational selection toward greater patience tied to fertility. He applies this reasoning to the UK Green Book as a case of current government practice.

name: Sadaf Basharat
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Sadaf Basharat's work focuses on measuring workplace well-being among early childhood education and care professionals in Norway. The publication uses psychometric methods, including factor analysis, reliability testing and comparison with related measures, applied to data from a randomized control trial. It evaluates the Workplace PERMA-Profiler and tests a revised set of Engagement items that make that dimension more distinct from Meaning.

name: Shuqi Wang
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Shuqi Wang studies investor behavior and trading performance in equity markets, using empirical analysis of large transaction datasets and regulatory changes as natural experiments. The work examines how the cost of acquiring information shapes retail investors' overconfidence, investor disagreement and stock mispricing, and compares the trading results of foreign and domestic investors in Indonesia. Applications lie in market regulation, disclosure policy and understanding differences in investor sophistication.

name: Simone Haeckl
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Simone Haeckl is an experimental economist who uses randomized field experiments, lab studies and large online experiments to study gender gaps, motivation and decision-making. Her work covers children's interest in STEM and methods for running school experiments, as well as leadership behaviors, team incentives and effort at work, and how people judge competitive behavior and assess their own ability. She also studies how information affects sustainable investment choices.

name: Sufyan Ullah Khan
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Sufyan Ullah Khan studies carbon emissions, environmental efficiency and sustainable development, mainly in China with some work in Pakistan. The publications use panel econometrics (threshold, spatial and time-series models), decomposition and frontier methods, interpretable machine learning, spatial analysis, farm surveys, discrete choice experiments and systematic literature review. Application areas include urban form and low-carbon cities, green finance and Industry 4.0, marine fisheries, agriculture and climate adaptation, biogas, food consumption and air pollution.

name: Torfinn Harding
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Torfinn Harding studies environmental and resource economics, focusing on how policy, taxation and governance shape deforestation and investment in natural resource sectors. His work uses quasi-experimental methods such as difference-in-differences, together with satellite-based spatial data and firm-level data, to examine conditional cash transfers in the Brazilian Amazon, forest loss around oil drilling worldwide, and the timing of tax deductions for petroleum exploration in Norway and the UK. He also looks at how multinational firms and public versus corporate governance relate to environmental outcomes.

name: Venke Furre Haaland
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Venke Furre Haaland is an economist whose work applies empirical causal methods to health care and education policy. Her publications use variation in hospital queue congestion to study how waiting for orthopedic surgery affects patients' health care use, work absence and disability receipt, and a large school field experiment to test whether adding a second teacher in early literacy classes improves learning. The work covers labor supply, public service delivery and differences in effects across student groups.

name: Wanwei He
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Wanwei He studies how ethically motivated investment exclusions affect stock returns and company behavior, using the divestment decisions of Norway's sovereign wealth fund as a case. The work compares the returns of excluded firms with those of firms later readmitted, tests whether the fund's actions can be linked causally to these patterns, and looks at how firms change their operations in response. The research sits in finance, with a focus on ESG investing, cost of capital and institutional investors.

name: Yuko Onozaka
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
summary: Yuko Onozaka studies how gender and diversity shape organizational outcomes, and how consumers make food choices. Her work uses regression analysis, linguistic analysis of meeting transcripts, choice experiments with latent class analysis, and think-aloud protocols combined with text mining. Application areas include central bank committee deliberations, women in leadership and digital transformation, and consumer preferences for farmed salmon in the USA, France and Japan.

name: Alberto Giacometti
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Alberto Giacometti studies how regional and territorial governance shapes green and just transition policy in Europe, covering the Nordic countries, Sweden's EU just transition planning and the Western Balkans. His work uses qualitative methods such as policy review, interviews and focus groups, along with conceptual and historical analysis, to examine transformative innovation policy, the evolution of the just green transition concept, and experimentalist macro-regional cooperation. The findings apply to regional development, climate and innovation policymaking in industrial regions and EU-linked policy settings.

name: Aldijana Bunjak
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Aldijana Bunjak studies leadership, employee well-being and innovation in organizations, with a focus on identity leadership, trust, mindfulness, burnout and technostress. Her work uses large multi-source and multilevel surveys, longitudinal and experimental designs, structural equation modeling, latent profile analysis and bibliometric reviews. Application areas include workplaces in German small and medium-sized enterprises, digital work environments, academic careers, and political and civic leadership across countries.

name: Ali Turkyilmaz
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Ali Turkyilmaz studies circular economy adoption in the construction industry, looking at costs and benefits, barriers, deconstruction and disassembly, digital tools, and tools for measuring circularity, mainly through stakeholder surveys, interviews, literature reviews and case studies. He also researches Industry 4.0 readiness and digital maturity in manufacturing firms, especially in Kazakhstan, using maturity models, structural equation modelling and advisory systems. Further work covers supply chain and inventory topics such as additive manufacturing in oil and gas and spare-parts forecasting in aviation, plus surveys on how home built environments affected remote work and study during COVID-19.

name: Andra Riandita
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Andra Riandita studies how firms use external collaboration and partnerships to pursue eco-innovation and sustainability goals. Methods include regression analysis of firm survey data, qualitative comparative analysis, content analysis of partnership data and multiple case studies. Application areas include Norwegian service firms, fashion and textile companies, food retailers, and alliances between established firms and green start-ups on food waste reduction.

name: Andres Rodriguez Pose
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Andres Rodriguez Pose studies how institutions, innovation and place shape regional development and territorial inequality, with a focus on the EU, China and other regions. His publications use panel econometrics, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, latent class and decision-tree models, as well as literature reviews and policy analysis. Application areas include EU Cohesion Policy, industrial policy, urban agglomeration, digital and AI technologies, the geography of science, and the political geography of discontent.

name: Annie Haver
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Annie Haver studies resilience, stress and mental wellbeing among older adult care workers, informal caregivers, and students in nursing and higher education. Her work uses systematic and qualitative reviews, interviews, cross-sectional surveys with moderation analyses, and a mixed-methods co-design project across seven countries to develop a digital toolbox for care leaders. She also examines emotion regulation and emotional intelligence in relation to stress and mental distress, and leadership competencies in the Norwegian hotel industry.

name: Auke Hunneman
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Auke Hunneman studies consumer and firm behavior in marketing and retail using quantitative models, including hierarchical Bayesian regression, spatial panel data models and survey experiments. The publications cover credit card delinquency prediction from combined credit and debit data, store location and sales forecasting for retail chains, consumer perception of packaging design, and how the speed of export entry relates to new venture survival.

name: Babusi Clint Ngwenya
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Babusi Clint Ngwenya studies how policy can drive the replacement of fossil fuel heating in existing buildings with heat pumps, focusing on Swiss cantons. The work combines semi-structured interviews on policy experience with comparisons of CO2 emissions across European countries and levelised cost and sensitivity analyses under different subsidy levels and energy price ratios. The findings are relevant to building owners, energy policymakers and regulators planning heating decarbonisation.

name: Bjørn Asheim
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Bjørn Asheim studies regional economic development, innovation and industrial change, with a focus on how human agency, institutions and policy shape new regional growth paths and sustainability transitions. His work combines theory building with interviews, long-running comparative case studies of Nordic regions, qualitative comparative analysis and policy document review. Application areas include oil and gas diversification into offshore wind and aquaculture in Norway, clusters and industrial districts, global production networks such as electric vehicle batteries, and transformative innovation policy.

name: Carina Antonia Hallin
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Carina Antonia Hallin studies collective intelligence and its use in democratic governance and public policymaking, including how citizen knowledge can be gathered through digital deliberation platforms combined with artificial intelligence and natural language processing. Her work includes edited handbook volumes, conceptual and commentary pieces on digital disruption and democratic values, and case studies such as a Danish municipality and a UN global platform. She has also published an automated machine learning method that uses k-means clustering to assign new observations to data clusters for recommendation and decision support.

name: Dahl Fitjar
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing

name: Espen Olsen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Espen Olsen studies how organisational climate, leadership and work conditions relate to safety, wellbeing and performance, mainly in hospitals but also in schools, small businesses and the wider Norwegian workforce. His work uses large survey datasets analysed with structural equation modelling, regression and longitudinal designs, alongside psychometric validation of the Norwegian Hospital Survey on Patient Safety Culture 2.0 and a systematic review of patient experience and outcomes. Topics include patient safety culture, remote work, personality, creativity, burnout and occupational health and safety management.

name: Farheen Naz
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Farheen Naz studies how digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data analytics and information and communication technologies support sustainable, resilient and smart supply chains and manufacturing. Her work combines systematic literature reviews, bibliometric analysis, structural topic modelling, meta-analysis, survey-based PLS-SEM and neural network modelling, and K-means clustering. Application areas include agriculture, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, carbon-neutral and net zero supply chains, circular economy, green consumer behaviour and renewable energy trends.

name: Fifi Tjan Kvalsvik
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Fifi Tjan Kvalsvik studies older adults living at home, covering both health care and consumer behaviour. One strand is a pre-post study protocol for interprofessional health needs assessment and frailty monitoring in Norwegian municipal care, combining quantitative measures of functional change with qualitative interviews. Another strand examines which situational factors, such as health, mobility and distance to a store, lead older adults to shop for groceries online, using interviews and a conjoint experiment.

name: Gro Ellen Mathisen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Gro Ellen Mathisen studies psychosocial work environment, safety and leadership, with a strong focus on high-risk industries such as Norway's offshore petroleum sector. Her work uses large national survey data, psychometric validation, systematic reviews, repeated-measures analysis, and qualitative interviews and focus groups, often drawing on the Job Demands-Resources model. Application areas include digitalization and organizational change in offshore work, speaking up about safety, older workers, hospitality, software engineering, and frontline leadership in implementing clinical guidelines in mental health services.

name: Hong Li
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Hong Li studies participatory and service design, with a focus on engaging stakeholders in digital health innovation, sustainable tourism and higher education. Her work relies on case studies and mixed methods such as interviews, observations, workshops, journey mapping, art-based methods and student reflections, set in settings including hospital remote care in China and Norway, tourism in Finland and campus sustainability in Norway. The publications address responsible technology adoption, service ecosystem cocreation, safety experience in services and student engagement through challenge-based learning.

name: Hongyan Shi
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Hongyan Shi studies pricing, product strategy and information decisions for firms and online platforms using game-theoretic analytical models. The publications examine whether a crowdsourcing platform should share style popularity information with artists who co-create products, and how technology for on-demand quality adjustments changes a firm's pricing and product-line choices under time-varying consumer needs. Outcomes analyzed include profit, consumer welfare and social welfare in digital and platform markets.

name: Huiwen Gong
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Huiwen Gong works in economic geography on how regions and firms build new industries, with a strong focus on China's electric vehicle battery sector and its expansion into Europe. Her work combines conceptual frameworks with qualitative case studies and interviews, and it also includes patent-data analysis of breakthrough innovation in US regions. Topics include global production networks and geoeconomics, regional resilience and innovation policy, green and just industrial transitions, interregional inequality, and catch-up in industries such as online games and blockchain.

name: Jinghua Xie
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Jinghua Xie studies the economics of tourism, hospitality and related consumer markets, with a focus on competition between Airbnb and hotels, hotel financial performance and survival, and seasonality. Methods include cointegration and threshold autoregressive models, panel data and hazard models, and logit and ordered-choice models applied to survey and firm-level data, mainly from Norway. Further work covers tourist knowledge, interest and satisfaction in whale watching and eco-certification, consumer preferences for live fish, destination resilience during COVID-19, and the social costs of electricity use.

name: Kai Victor Myrnes-Hansen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kai Victor Myrnes-Hansen studies how people experience and assess smell disorders, food and meals, and healthcare services, with a focus on olfactory dysfunction after COVID-19, food for older adults, and video consultations. His methods include expert interviews, systematic reviews, focus groups, grounded theory, and survey-based cluster analysis. The work is applied to clinical assessment tools, institutional food and elderly care, and telemedicine practice in the Nordic countries.

name: Kjersti Berge Evensen
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kjersti Berge Evensen studies oral health and health services for vulnerable groups, including people with dental anxiety, survivors of abuse or torture, and prisoners. Her work combines questionnaire-based statistical analyses, qualitative interviews, realist evaluation and literature reviews to examine anxiety, quality of life, health literacy and access to care. She also develops and tests survey instruments on information sharing between health and kitchen personnel in hospitals and nursing homes.

name: Kristina Nilsson Lindström
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Kristina Nilsson Lindström studies how governance can support the development of popular culture tourism, a niche form of tourism, within regional development and the sustainability transition. Her work draws on a selective literature review to propose a meta-governance analytic framework, which looks at the rationale for the tourism, stakeholders, the governance landscape, and the strategies and tools used. The framework is intended for theoretical and empirical examination of existing and future tourism governance at regional level.

name: Lukasz Andrzej Derdowski
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Lukasz Andrzej Derdowski studies how people's perceptions, attitudes and work conditions shape behavior in organizational and consumer settings, covering responsible leadership, sustainable consumption, and workplace safety. His methods include survey-based measurement and index development, structural equation modeling, topic modeling of interviews, and systematic literature review. Application areas include leadership and trust in service organizations, social marketing and policy for consumption reduction, and psychosocial risk in high-risk industries.

name: Marte C  W Solheim
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Marte C W Solheim studies innovation and entrepreneurship, with a focus on how collaboration, geography, regional policy and organisational factors shape eco-innovation, digital innovation, agility and industrial restructuring, mainly in Norway. Her work uses firm surveys, structural equation modelling, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, interviews, document analysis, case studies and literature reviews. Further publications cover smart specialisation, gender and migrant inclusion in venture capital and labour markets, creativity in small firms, smart-city partnerships and higher education policy.

name: Matthew Mark Coffay
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Matthew Mark Coffay studies circular economy and sustainable business model innovation, including how circular business models emerge and how policy in the EU and California shapes company strategies in the United States. His work draws on interviews, workshops, case studies, literature review and design science to build frameworks and practitioner tools for organizational design, dynamic capabilities and circular experimentation. Further application areas include Norwegian aquaculture, CRISPR salmon innovation and responsible innovation for sustainability impact assessment.

name: Muzamil Farooq
faculty: UiS School of Business and Law
department: Department of Innovation, Management and Marketing
summary: Muzamil Farooq studies how regional development can be examined through a future-oriented lens, moving beyond explanations based on path dependence and structural analysis. His work compares eight methodological approaches, grouped into three clusters and assessed by purpose, techniques, data needs and user suitability, to form a varied toolbox for regional futures research.
